summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Aldi has been crowned the winner of a major Christmas cheese taste test, beating household names including Cathedral City, M&S and Waitrose with an extra mature cheddar costing just £2.99. The supermarket's Specially Selected West Country Extra Mature Cheddar scored an impressive 78% in a blind taste test conducted by consumer champion Which?, earning its coveted Best Buy and Great Value awards. Experts praised the cheese for its smooth, firm and creamy texture, with Aldi's offering coming out ahead of 10 other popular supermarket and branded cheddars. It even managed to beat Cathedral City's Extra Mature Cheddar, which scored 74%, while M&S's Cornish Cruncher Extra Mature Cheddar received 70%. At £2.99 for a 350g block, Aldi's award-winning cheese could be a cheaper way for shoppers to stock up ahead of Christmas and add a crowd-pleasing option to their festive cheeseboard. The cheddar is available in Aldi stores nationwide now, ahead of the supermarket's wider Christmas cheese range arriving on November 25. Aldi's £2.99 extra mature cheddar has beaten Cathedral City, M&S and Waitrose (Image: Aldi) Which? blind-tested 11 extra mature cheddars, assessing them with a panel of experts and consumers. Aldi came out on top with 78%, ahead of several well-known brands and supermarket own-label alternatives. The full rankings were: Julie Ashfield, Chief Commercial Officer at Aldi UK, said: “We’re delighted to see our Specially Selected West Country Extra Mature Cheddar recognised by Which? as a Best Buy. “We know how important quality and value are, particularly at Christmas, and this award is a fantastic result for our team. “At just £2.99, shoppers can enjoy an award-winning cheddar that delivers on both taste and value, making it a great addition to any festive cheeseboard.” The award-winning cheddar is just one of the products in Aldi's wider Christmas cheese collection, which launches in stores from November 25 and will be available throughout December. Among the highlights are: Aldi's Specially Selected West Country Extra Mature Cheddar is available in stores now for £2.99, while the wider Christmas cheese, chutney, cracker and flavoured butter range arrives from November 25. Recommended reading: According to the Coupon Kid, Jordon Cox: "Aldi & Catherdral City cheese are made in the SAME factory - here’s how you can tell. "On the back of all dairy & meat items in the UK, you’ll find an oval code - that tells you the factory that it was made from. All products are required to have this. The Cathedral City factory is an award winning creamery in Davidstow - with the code NU007. "And guess what code Aldi’s own brand cheese also has on the back..? Yep. NU007." But, he adds: "Now - before you all start coming at me in the comments, I’m FULLY aware that this doesn’t mean it’s the same cheese. And they may use different ingredients. "But, if the quality is so high at that factory (as Cathedral City themselves say), then the Aldi cheese should be a good alternative, and save you £1 every time you buy some cheese!"

metadata.title: BBC announces Christmas line-up with Ncuti Gatwa, Bill Nighy and huge Hollywood stars
metadata.contentSnippet: BBC Christmas radio schedule features Ncuti Gatwa, Bill Nighy, Macaulay Culkin and a George Michael tribute across Radio 4, Radio 2, Radio 1 and Sounds.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: BBC announces Christmas line-up with Ncuti Gatwa, Bill Nighy and huge Hollywood stars
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Ncuti Gatwa and Bill Nighy will feature in BBC Radio’s seasonal line-up. The broadcaster has announced a packed schedule of audio dramas, special programmes and playlists across BBC Radio and BBC Sounds for the festive season, including a new adaptation of Peter Pan starring Gatwa as Captain Hook. The Radio 4 drama will air later this year alongside Greatest Living Writer, an audio sitcom featuring Bill Nighy and written by director and screenwriter Richard Curtis. Curtis and Nighy have previously collaborated on films such as Love Actually and About Time. Listeners can also look forward to Christmas editions of Radio 4’s Desert Island Discs, with guests including This Country star Daisy May Cooper, Alien actress Sigourney Weaver and musician Peter Gabriel. Other highlights include a Christmas Eve takeover of Radio 2 by Home Alone actor Macaulay Culkin, Beverley Knight’s Great British Gospel Christmas, and a special edition of Uncanny Christmas Case Book with Sir Lenny Henry. A celebration of George Michael’s life and music will also air across BBC Sounds, Radio 4 and Radio 2, marking 10 years since his passing on Christmas Day. On Radio 1, listeners will hear the announcement of the UK’s official Christmas number one. Kate Phillips, BBC chief content officer, said: "Christmas on BBC Radio and BBC Sounds is all about the moments that bring us together. "Whether, in the words of the unforgettable Chris Rea, you’re driving home for Christmas, celebrating with loved ones, working through the festive season, or taking a much needed breather, we’ll be there with the very best music, laughter, live sport, enchanting storytelling and festive specials. "From world-class performances to unforgettable shared moments, BBC Radio and BBC Sounds will be with audiences throughout Christmas and New Year, soundtracking the celebrations and providing companionship when it matters most." BBC Sounds will also offer a festive selection of podcasts and shows, including Laura Whitmore and Iain Stirling’s Murder They Wrote and a Christmas special of Sidetracked with Nick Grimshaw and Annie Macmanus.

metadata.title: UK greeting card and party supplies company enters administration after 42 years
metadata.contentSnippet: Tiger Feet entered administration on November 17 after 42 years, and while it continues to trade, customers are warned: "All sales are final".

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: UK greeting card and party supplies company enters administration after 42 years
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A UK greeting card and party supplies company has entered administration after 42 years in business. Tiger Feet began as Budget Greeting Cards in 1984, offering greeting cards, partyware, balloons, stationery, and toys (before being rebranded in 2024). The company has since developed into a major UK wholesaler supplying more than 20,000 products to independent retailers across the UK and Ireland. Tiger Feet operates online and from seven cash and carry sites located across the UK and Ireland: Now, after 42 years in business, Tiger Feet has entered administration. Anthony Collier and Richard Goodall of FRP Advisory Trading Limited were appointed joint administrators on November 17. In a statement published by Business Sale Report (BSR), the administrators said: "Tiger Feet has an established position in the wholesale market and a long history of supplying independent retailers across the UK and Ireland. "Our priority is to maintain trading while we continue to explore options available for the business, we would encourage any interested parties to contact us as soon as possible." A notice on the Tiger Feet website confirms it is in administration and continues to trade under the management of the joint administrators. The statement reads: "Tiger Feet Ltd UK (01798438) entered Administration on 17 November 2026. "The affairs, business and property of the Company are being managed by the appointed Joint Administrators Anthony Collier and Richard Goodall both of FRP Advisory Trading Limited. "The business is continuing to trade. "The Joint Administrators act as agents of the Company and without personal liability." Tiger Feet has warned customers it is no longer offering refunds or returns, stating that "all sales are final." Customers have been advised to check goods carefully before purchase at cash and carry branches, as all items are sold "as seen and as available." For online orders, customers are instructed to report missing or damaged items within two days of receipt. The company added: "Tiger Feet Limited does not provide refunds, returns, exchanges, credit notes, warranty claims, repair or replacement services." It has been a tough year for the UK high street, with several retailers entering administration or liquidation and others announcing widespread store closures. Major high street brands Claire's and Quiz have been forced to close all their remaining stores after falling into administration. UK fashion retailer Leading Labels is also set to close its remaining 15 stores after falling into liquidation in May. Whitbread closed all its standalone branded restaurants across the UK last month, affecting five brands: However, Queensway Inns and Common Table Group have now taken over 110 of these former Whitbread sites, saving them from closure. Poundland has filed a notice to appoint administrators, putting the future of its 150 stores and 11,000 employees at risk. TG Jones and the British Heart Foundation will also be closing around 150 stores each across the UK. Wynsors World of Shoes is shutting 17 stores across the UK, with closing down sales already underway at several affected branches. UK entertainment retailer Zavvi has ceased trading after nearly 20 years, having collapsed into administration for a second time. Australian stationery retailer Typo is also set to pull out of the UK in 2027, closing all its stores and ending online trading. Other retailers have been forced to close stores this year, including: Several UK travel companies have ceased trading or entered administration in 2026, including: Wayfairer Travel Limited has also suspended all services "until further notice" as it looks to appoint an administrator. Meanwhile, five UK airlines have fallen into administration or liquidation: UK delivery company Yodel was phased out completely in July after being acquired by InPost. Iconic fashion brand Nasty Gal has also shut down its website after being sold by Debenhams in a deal worth around £12 million (US$16 million). It hasn't all been bad news for the UK high street, with several major brands announcing new store openings for 2026, including Joules, B&M, Aldi, M&S, and Superdrug. Meanwhile, brands including Evans and Bodycare have returned to the UK high street this year after previously closing all their stores. Have you ever purchased a greeting card or party supplies from Tiger Feet? Let us know in the poll above or in the comments below.

metadata.title: Greggs warns festive item will sell out this weekend and not return until 2027
metadata.contentSnippet: Greggs has shared that the Sweet Mince Pie Roll is likely to sell out by November 28/29 and won't be back until winter 2027

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Greggs warns festive item will sell out this weekend and not return until 2027
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Greggs has warned customers that one of its festive items is predicted to sell out by this weekend, and it won't be available in shops again until next year. The retailer unveiled its new Christmas menu back in October, and one of the items included was the Sweet Mince Pie Roll. This is filled with sweet mincemeat made from vine fruits, Bramley apples and candied orange and lemon peel, wrapped in puff pastry and finished with a light dusting of icing sugar. Greggs says the sweet treat, which costs £1, has quickly become a fan favourite, but it is predicted to sell out by this weekend (Saturday, November 28 and Sunday, November 29). The Sweet Mince Pie Roll was introduced along with other Greggs Christmas menu items back in October (Image: Greggs) It has been confirmed that once the Sweet Mince Pie Roll sells out, it will not return until the winter season of 2027. Zoe Harris, Customer Director at Greggs, said: "The Sweet Mince Pie Roll has quickly become one of the stars of our Christmas menu, but they’ve proven so popular that we’re set to sell out before December. "So, consider this a public service announcement, this is the last week to get your hands on one before it disappears until next Christmas. "As for Santa, if he misses out this week, our classic Sweet Mince Pies are still in stock and waiting for him." Earlier this month, Greggs opened a luxury hotel suite in partnership with Hotel Gotham in Newcastle. The Greggs Suite, designed for two guests, offers year-round stays. Decorated in Greggs’ signature midnight blue and gold, the suite features a 'ring for a sausage roll' concierge service. Guests can use a dedicated rotary phone to order Greggs favourites, which will be delivered to the room on a silver platter. Recommended reading: Those staying during the first 96 days will also receive limited-edition Greggs merchandise, including bespoke dressing gowns, slippers, and eye masks. A portion of proceeds from each stay will be donated annually to the Greggs Foundation to support local community initiatives and schools via the Feeding Brighter Futures programme. Reservations for the Greggs Suite are available to book on the Gotham Hotel website. Have you tried the Sweet Mince Pie Roll, and what did you think of it? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: Jury retires to consider verdict in trial of Huntingdon train attacker
metadata.contentSnippet: A jury has retired to consider whether a knifeman who stabbed multiple people on board an LNER train in Huntingdon is guilty of attempted murder.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Jury retires to consider verdict in trial of Huntingdon train attacker
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A jury has retired to consider whether a knifeman who stabbed multiple people on board a train in Cambridgeshire is guilty of attempted murder. Several people were injured on an LNER train from Doncaster to London King's Cross on November 1, 2025, which was forced to make an emergency stop at Huntingdon. Anthony Williams, 33, denies 14 counts of attempted murder: ten of them in relation to the LNER train, three said to have happened in Peterborough and one at Pontoon Dock DLR station in London. However, Williams has pleaded guilty to wounding with intent, among a handful of other offences including affray. The attempted murder trial began at Cambridge Crown Court on October 28. Williams attended court via video link from Rampton Hospital in Nottinghamshire and did not give evidence. On November 23, at around 2.50pm, the jury of nine men and three women retired to consider their verdict after hearing weeks of evidence from in-person witnesses, read statements and video recorded interviews. In his summing up of the case, the judge, Mr Justice Calver, told the jury: "What you must do is consider all of the evidence separately in relation to each count. "You must not speculate about what the evidence may tell you." He told jurors that a unanimous verdict is needed and that they should put the idea of a majority verdict "completely out of your mind". Mr Calver said that jurors are under no time pressure and should take as much time as they need to come to a decision. There are only two possible verdicts for each count, he added, guilty or not guilty.

metadata.title: Cambridgeshire mayor backs Great Ouse Valley Heritage Landscape bid
metadata.contentSnippet: The mayor of Cambridge and Peterborough has pledged support to the Great Ouse Valley Trust (GOVT).

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire mayor backs Great Ouse Valley Heritage Landscape bid
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The mayor of Cambridge and Peterborough has pledged support to the Great Ouse Valley Trust (GOVT). Mayor Paul Bristow confirmed his commitment to the Trust’s ambition to self-designate the Great Ouse Valley Heritage Landscape. His announcement came after addressing a room of the trust’s stakeholder delegates in the St Ives Corn Exchange. At the meeting, the mayor listened to presentations from key figures who have played a pivotal role in advancing the trust's objectives. These included the GOVT chair, Graham Campbell, community engagement specialist Dr Jade Gunnell, and Jon Sheaff, director of Arkwood Landscape Architects. The mayor said: "The landscape is absolutely beautiful and a truly special part of our region. "I fully support their (GOVT) efforts to self-designate … and the formation of the Partnership. "I am putting my Mayoral Authority right behind these efforts." Arkwood had been commissioned to produce a Business Study case for the designation, which clearly demonstrated benefits for all, especially from tourism. The Arkwood report has won Best Project in this year’s Planning Excellence Awards from the Royal Town Planning Institute and Best in Planning and Landscape Assessment from the Landscape Institute. During the meeting, Dr Gunnell distributed ‘Call to Action’ cards, requesting delegates to note pledges that could help the trust advance the designation effort. The mayor was the first to fill out his card, which he then raised in the air, concluding his speech with the words "Let’s get it done!" This move provides the trust with the required evidence of support and commitment for the creation of a funded partnership board to manage and promote the landscape area. As this aligns with the mayor’s own Local Visitor Economy Partnership initiative for both Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, the trust’s ambition for a Heritage Landscape designation could soon become a reality. For more information about the Great Ouse Valley Trust’s work, visit www.greatousevalletrust.org.uk.

metadata.title: The stunning National Trust site in Cambridgeshire perfect for a day out
metadata.contentSnippet: Tucked away on the banks of the River Great Ouse, Houghton Mill is home stunning scenery and wildlife-rich habitats.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: The stunning National Trust site in Cambridgeshire perfect for a day out
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Tucked away on the banks of the River Great Ouse, this National Trust site is among Cambridgeshire's underrated attractions. Overshadowed by some of the region's larger historic sites, this riverside retreat combines heritage, wildlife and scenic walking routes. At the heart of the site is Houghton Mill, the last surviving working watermill on the River Great Ouse. Visitors can explore the historic building and discover how grain was transformed into flour using traditional machinery, with volunteer millers helping bring centuries of history to life. During the operating season, the giant waterwheel can still be seen turning, offering a glimpse into a way of life that once powered communities across the country. Beyond the mill lies the beautiful Waterclose Meadows, a landscape of riverside grassland, wildlife-rich habitats and tranquil walking paths. Footpaths lead through the meadows and along the river towards the picturesque villages of The Hemingfords, making it a favourite spot for walkers, photographers and nature lovers. In summer, the meadows buzz with insects and birds, while the river provides a constantly changing backdrop. Despite its rural atmosphere, visitors will find plenty of amenities. The on-site tea room enjoys a picturesque riverside location and serves freshly made cakes, scones, light lunches, hot drinks and seasonal treats. Indoor and outdoor seating allows visitors to relax beside the water after exploring the site. There is also parking, a gift shop, toilet facilities and accessible routes around much of the property. Families are well catered for, with open green spaces, picnic areas and easy riverside walks providing plenty of opportunities to enjoy the outdoors together. The site is also popular with cyclists thanks to nearby links with the wider cycle network. For those looking to discover a quieter side of Cambridgeshire, Houghton Mill and Waterclose Meadows offers history, scenery and relaxation in equal measure. It may be one of the county's hidden gems, but once visited, it is unlikely to remain a secret for long. Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: 'Can you be sure he intended to kill?' judge asks jurors in train attack trial
metadata.contentSnippet: Judge Mr Justice Calver in the trial of Anthony Williams, accused of attempted murder on an LNER train in Huntingdon, has told the jury to consider intent.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 'Can you be sure he intended to kill?' judge asks jurors in train attack trial
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The judge in the trial of a knifeman accused of attempted murder on a train in Cambridgeshire has told the jury to consider whether they can be sure he intended to kill. Several people were injured on an LNER train from Doncaster to London King's Cross on November 1, 2025, which was forced to make an emergency stop in Huntingdon. Anthony Williams, 33, denies 14 counts of attempted murder: ten of them in relation to the LNER train, three said to have happened in Peterborough and one at Pontoon Dock DLR station in London. Anthony Williams is accused of 14 counts of attempted murder (Image: British Transport) The judge, Mr Justice Calver, began his summing up of the case at Cambridge Crown Court on November 23. In the case of count one, Williams is accused of attempting to murder a 14-year-old boy, who legally cannot be named, by a footbridge near Henry Penn Walk in Peterborough on October 31, 2025. The boy, who was walking there with a friend, was treated in hospital for a single stab wound two to three centimetres to the left of his breastbone. Mr Justice Calver told the jury that while the prosecution relies on the force and location of the stab wound showing intent to kill, the defence suggests a single stab wound does not show intention to kill. In the case of count two, Williams is accused of attempting to murder Dawid Taborski in the same area of Henry Penn Walk. Mr Justice Calver told the jury Mr Taborski said "I literally ran for my life", adding that prosecutor Christopher Paxton KC suggests this showed clear intent to kill as it was only because the victim was young, fit and ran for his life that he was not struck. He said that defence barrister Gillian Jones relies on the fact there was no physical contact, he did not attempt to run after Mr Taborski and his friend and the incident was consistent with Williams' psychotic state. In the case of count three, Williams is accused of attempting to murder William Ogelby in the Rail World car park in Peterborough. Mr Justice Calver told the jury that Mr Ogelby said: "I thought he was going to kill me" and added that the defendant tried to go for his chest. He said the defence suggests the victim's perception that he was going to be killed "should be considered with caution" as this does not show what was going on in the defendant's mind, and that the jury cannot be sure he intended to kill. The court heard that Williams arrived at Ritzy Barbers in Peterborough, which is around a ten minute walk away, at 7.20pm. Mr Justice Calver said the court has heard that Williams was waving a knife around inside the shop and the incident is captured on CCTV. Williams has pleaded guilty to affray regarding this incident. CCTV footage shows Anthony Williams brandishing a knife inside the Ritzy Barbers in Peterborough (Image: BTP/Press Association) CCTV footage issued by British Transport Police showing Anthony Williams brandishing a knife inside the Ritzy Barbers in Peterborough (Image: BTP/Press Association) The court heard that Williams then got a taxi back to his home address and threw the knife into his back garden, before travelling to Peterborough train station at 8.17pm and catching a southbound train to Stevenage. He stole knives from an Asda store in Stevenage before getting on another train to London and subsequent Underground services, jurors heard. CCTV footage shows Anthony Williams in the Asda store in Stevenage (Image: BTP/Press Association) In the case of count four, Williams is accused of attempting to murder 17-year-old Isaiah Idris on a DLR train at Pontoon Dock. The judge told the jury that the prosecution suggest Williams waited for the train doors to close and the striking of Isaiah's head shows intent to kill. However, Mr Justice Calver added, the defence dispute this, suggesting it was a quick slashing action and Williams was likely suffering from auditory hallucinations. CCTV footage dated issued by British Transport Police shows Anthony Williams with a knife on board a DLR train travelling towards Pontoon Dock in London (Image: BTP/Press Association) Continuing his summing up of the case, Mr Calver said the court heard Williams travelled back to Peterborough on trains, making stops at Stevenage and Hitchin, and returned to his home address before boarding the LNER service to London King's Cross at 7.26pm on November 1, 2025. Williams boarding a train at Stevenage (Image: BTP/Press Association) The remaining ten counts of attempted murder concern passengers on the train, namely Jonathan Gjoshe, Sachin Balakrishnan, David Presland, Scott Bletcher, Scott Green, Kevin Deely, Stephen Crean, Raza Aslam, Michael Paffett and Samir Zitouni. In each case, Mr Calver reminded jurors that they must prove intent to kill. Williams has already admitted to wounding with intent. Mr Calver asked jurors: "When he stabbed Mr Green three times with the knife, can you be sure he intended to kill him?" He told the court that prosecutor Christopher Paxton KC called the final three counts "one continuous attack with the intention to kill each of these victims." CCTV footage shows Anthony Williams brandishing a knife on an LNER Doncaster to London service (Image: BTP/Press Association) Dr Bernard Chin, a consultant forensic psychiatrist, diagnosed Williams with schizophrenia and said while he was likely suffering from "thought broadcast", where one experiences thoughts being said out loud to them, among other symptoms, he is not clinically insane. The jury of nine men and three women retired to consider their verdict at around 2.50pm on Monday, November 23. Mr Justice Calver told the jury: "What you must do is consider all of the evidence separately in relation to each count. "You must not speculate about what the evidence may tell you." Mr Calver said that jurors are under no time pressure and should take as much time as they need to come to a decision. The trial continues.

metadata.title: DWP Cold Weather Payments - Who gets the money and how does it work?
metadata.contentSnippet: With the Met Office warning of freezing temperatures, the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) may soon be issuing Cold Weather Payments.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: DWP Cold Weather Payments - Who gets the money and how does it work?
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: With temperatures set to plummet across Norfolk, the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) may soon be issuing Cold Weather Payments to eligible households. The payments are available to some people receiving certain benefits when the area where they live experiences a sustained period of freezing weather. But a brief cold snap or a single freezing night will not necessarily lead to a payment. Here is everything you need to know about Cold Weather Payments, including who qualifies, how they are triggered and when the money should arrive. Cold Weather Payments are intended to help eligible households with additional costs during sustained periods of very cold weather. A payment is triggered when the average temperature in a person’s area is recorded as, or forecast to be, 0C or below for seven consecutive days. The scheme runs between November 1 and March 31, 2027. It is important to note that the payment is based on the average temperature across a full seven-day period, rather than an individual cold day or night. Eligible recipients receive £25 for each qualifying seven-day period of very cold weather. This means someone could receive more than one payment during the winter if there are several qualifying periods. For example, one qualifying seven-day period would result in a £25 payment. Two qualifying periods would result in £50 and three qualifying periods would result in £75. Cold Weather Payments do not affect a person’s entitlement to other benefits. People may qualify if they receive one of the following: The precise conditions depend on the benefit being received. People receiving Pension Credit will usually qualify for Cold Weather Payments. If a qualifying spell of cold weather is recorded in their area, the payment should be issued automatically. People will usually qualify if they receive income-related Employment and Support Allowance and are in either the work-related activity group or support group. Those who are not in either group may still qualify if they have: Universal Credit claimants will usually qualify if neither they nor their partner is employed or considered “gainfully self-employed”. They must also meet at least one of the following conditions: Someone is likely to be considered gainfully self-employed if self-employment is their main job, they work regularly and they expect to make a profit. Universal Credit claimants can also qualify if their award includes a disabled child amount. In this situation, it does not matter whether they or their partner are working, self-employed or unemployed. People receiving Support for Mortgage Interest may qualify if they are treated as receiving a qualifying benefit and one of the following applies: A person may be treated as receiving a qualifying benefit if they applied for it but did not receive it because their income was too high. Eligible people do not normally need to make a claim because Cold Weather Payments are issued automatically. Universal Credit or income-related Employment and Support Allowance claimants should report it if they have had a baby or if a child aged under five has come to live with them. Universal Credit claimants can report the change through their online account, while people receiving income-related Employment and Support Allowance should contact Jobcentre Plus. Failure to report the change could mean a payment is not issued automatically. The money should reach an eligible recipient within 14 working days of the end of each qualifying seven-day period. It is paid into the same bank or building society account used for the person’s benefit payments.

metadata.title: UK rents forecast to rise twice as fast as house prices over the next 3 years
metadata.contentSnippet: Hamptons forecasts UK rents will rise 14.2% by 2029, twice as fast as house prices, while Lloyds finds buying cheaper than renting in seven cities.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: UK rents forecast to rise twice as fast as house prices over the next 3 years
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Rents are expected to rise around twice as fast as house prices. Newly-let properties are forecast to see this surge over the next three years, according to Hamptons. The property company predicts that across Britain, private rents for newly-let homes will increase by 14.2% between the fourth quarter of 2026 and the fourth quarter of 2029. In comparison, house prices are expected to grow by a more modest 7.2% over the same period. Hamptons attributes the rising rents to a limited supply of rental properties and ongoing affordability challenges for first-time buyers. Aneisha Beveridge, head of research at Hamptons, said: "With fewer homes entering the rental market, competition between tenants is likely to keep rents rising faster than house prices over the next few years. "For landlords, that creates a delicate balancing act because higher costs do not automatically translate into higher rents. "Historically, landlords have had limited scope to pass those costs on, with rents set by wider market conditions rather than their individual bills. "But as costs have risen across the sector and rental supply has fallen, the bar has shifted, allowing more of those increases to feed through into higher rents. "There is, however, a silver lining for investors. "With rents rising faster than house prices, yields are improving, particularly across parts of southern England. "In London, that has already started to tempt some landlords back into the market. "For tenants, though, a smaller rental market means more competition and continued pressure on affordability. "Existing tenants may initially be more insulated from rising rents, but the new-let and existing-tenancy markets do not operate independently. "Over time, stronger new-let rental growth is likely to filter through to the wider market." Hamptons expects rents on all privately rented homes—not just newly-let properties—to rise by 10.9% over the next three years. The firm said rent growth on newly-agreed lets could begin to slow in 2028 and 2029 as mortgage rates are expected to decline. However, many long-term challenges in the rental sector are likely to persist. In a separate report, Lloyds analysed the cost of buying versus renting in 12 major UK cities and found that owning a home could be cheaper than renting in seven of them. The analysis was based on Office for National Statistics (ONS) data and assumed a 5% deposit. Lloyds' research indicated that in Glasgow, buyers could save £288 per month compared to renters. In Newcastle, the monthly saving was estimated at £187, while in Bristol, buyers could save £139 per month. Andrew Asaam, mortgages director at Lloyds, said: "Higher mortgage rates have seen the cost of borrowing increase this year, making that affordability calculation even more important. "But in many cities across the UK, buyers could still pay less for their mortgage than they would typically be charged in rent – giving them an immediate saving as well as a place of their own." Meanwhile, property consultancy Knight Frank has revised its UK house price forecasts downward. It now expects house price growth of just 1% in 2027, down from the 3% forecasted in April. Knight Frank said that cumulative UK house price growth over the five years to 2031 is now expected to reach 14.2%, compared to its previous estimate of 20.4%. The downgrade reflects concerns about the political climate, higher borrowing costs, and ongoing geopolitical instability, all of which are expected to dampen buyer demand and market confidence.

metadata.title: Post Office warns Christmas shoppers to post early ahead of busiest parcel day
metadata.contentSnippet: Post Office expects December 7 to be its busiest Christmas parcel day, with more than 100m items expected.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Post Office warns Christmas shoppers to post early ahead of busiest parcel day
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Monday, December 7, is expected to be the Post Office’s busiest day for sending festive parcels. With customers across the UK preparing to post gifts to loved ones both domestically and overseas, the Post Office anticipates handling more than 100 million parcels during the two-month Christmas period. Shanaz Nandha, postmaster at Biggleswade Post Office, said: "Christmas is always a busy time for us in branch, with lots of customers sending presents to friends and family across the UK and overseas." The Post Office is encouraging people to post early wherever possible, especially for international deliveries. While Monday December 7 is forecast to be peak posting day, the Post Office said it is reminding customers they do not need to wait until the busiest period. Popular overseas destinations for Christmas parcels include the United States, Australia, Ireland, Germany and Poland. The Post Office suggested that people check last posting dates, particularly if they are sending items overseas. Royal Mail has also published its recommended last posting dates for UK services: December 19 is also the last posting date for Royal Mail Tracked Returns 48 to reach the sender before Christmas. The Post Office advises customers to check their branch's final acceptance time, which varies between branches. Royal Mail says its published dates are subject to change and advises customers to post as early as possible. It also recommends sending international items early, with published delivery aims available in its country guides.

metadata.title: Further details emerge after armed police descend on Cambridgeshire village
metadata.contentSnippet: Two boys have been arrested after armed police descended on the Brookland Centre in Sutton, near Ely.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Further details emerge after armed police descend on Cambridgeshire village
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The reason why armed police descended on a quiet Cambridgeshire village has been revealed. It follows reports that officers had descended at the Royal British Legion in Sutton, near Ely, on Saturday (November 21). In an update today, Cambridgeshire Police confirmed it attended the Brookland Centre and arrested two boys. A 15-year-old boy from St Ives has since been charged with taking a vehicle without consent, theft, and possession of a knife. He is also accused of driving without a licence or insurance and is due to appear at Huntingdon Magistrates’ Court on February 3, 2026. A 17-year-old boy from Ely has since been charged with two counts of theft. He is due to appear at Cambridge Magistrates’ Court on January 14, 2026, a spokesperson for the force confirmed. metadata.title: Huntingdon men urged to register with a GP and seek help early this Movember
metadata.contentSnippet: Priory Fields Surgery is urging men to prioritise their health this Movember by registering with a GP and getting any concerns checked early.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Huntingdon men urged to register with a GP and seek help early this Movember
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Priory Fields Surgery is urging men to prioritise their health this Movember by registering with a GP and getting any concerns checked early. The Huntingdon practice is calling on men across the town and surrounding villages to take action, especially during Movember, which raises awareness of prostate cancer, testicular cancer, mental health and suicide prevention. In the UK, one in eight men will be diagnosed with prostate cancer in their lifetime, rising to one in four for Black men. Dr Chris Smith, GP partner at Priory Fields Surgery, said: "Too many men wait until something is really wrong before they come and see us. "We'd much rather see you early, when we can help most. "Whether it's a quick blood pressure check, a worry you've been putting off or how you're feeling in yourself, please don't sit on it. "And if you're not registered with a GP yet, now is the time to do it. "It only takes a few minutes, and you can even contact us online without picking up the phone." The surgery highlighted that men are generally less likely than women to see a GP and often delay seeking help until symptoms become more serious. Early prostate cancer often shows no symptoms, so men over 50, those with a family history of the disease, and Black men are especially encouraged to speak to their GP about their risk. Men are also advised not to ignore changes such as a lump in the testicles, altered toilet habits, unexplained weight loss or persistent tiredness. Regular blood pressure checks are also important, as high blood pressure usually has no symptoms. The surgery is currently welcoming new patients from Huntingdon and nearby villages. Registration can be completed online in just a few minutes. Priory Fields also offers the Ask My GP online contact service, allowing patients to reach the practice without needing to call. Meanwhile, Dr Duncan Blake from the surgery has been invited to discuss men's health on Ouse Valley Radio’s Over to You programme. To register, visit www.prioryfieldssurgery.nhs.uk/practice-information/new-patients.

metadata.title: World’s largest AI breast cancer trial launches in Cambridgeshire
metadata.contentSnippet: Cambridgeshire is the first UK location to launch a major AI-assisted NHS breast screening trial involving 700,000 women.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: World’s largest AI breast cancer trial launches in Cambridgeshire
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A landmark Cambridgeshire trial is testing whether artificial intelligence can detect breast cancer earlier. The study, funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR), will involve around 700,000 women at 30 sites and is the world’s largest of its kind. The trial will test an AI tool that helps specialists review mammograms. Health Secretary Yvette Cooper launched the study during a visit to Addenbrooke’s Hospital. Patient Shirley meeting Yvette Cooper, Secretary of State for Health and Social Care (Image: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust/Mel Yeneralski) Ms Cooper said: "This is the biggest AI breast cancer trial in the world, backed by £10 million of government investment to speed up diagnosis and potentially deliver life-saving improvements. "If successful, this technology could help women get a breast cancer diagnosis and start treatment much more quickly, giving them the best possible chance of recovery." Women aged 50 to 71 across the UK are invited for breast screening every three years, with around 2.1 million screenings each year. Two specialist radiologists review each mammogram, although fewer than one per cent show signs of cancer. A set of mammogram images showing a pair of breasts from two different angles. The black and white image has been annotated by the AI tool to indicate where cancer may be. (Image: The EDITH team) The EDITH trial will use the AI tool alongside clinicians to spot cancers that might otherwise be missed because they are too small. If successful, the tool could mean some mammograms need only one radiologist’s review, freeing clinicians to focus on diagnosis and patient care. Shirley, 70, from Cambridgeshire, welcomed the trial after a routine screening found her early-stage breast cancer in October 2025, although she is not taking part. Shirley outside Addenbrooke’s Hospital. (Image: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust/Mel Yeneralski) She said: "I feel so lucky my cancer was detected early. "When I received the invitation to attend, I had no symptoms and no clue anything was wrong. "My routine mammogram saved my life, so anything that helps other people get diagnosed earlier is crucial. "That's why this trial is so important." Shirley at the cancer screening van in Trumpington, Cambridge where she has the screening scan that diagnosed her breast cancer in 2025. (Image: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust/Mel Yeneralski) The AI tool will not change the screening appointment, but it may change how the images are reviewed. All mammograms will continue to be reviewed by at least one human radiologist. Professor Fiona Gilbert, from the Department of Radiology at the University of Cambridge and an honorary consultant at Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, said: "Millions of women have a mammogram each year, and fewer than one in 100 will be diagnosed with cancer. "EDITH will test whether an AI-assisted mammogram-reading tool can help experts review images more efficiently, while maintaining professional oversight and the standards women expect from NHS breast screening." Professor Sian Taylor-Phillips, NIHR research professor and professor of population health at the University of Warwick, said: "EDITH will test whether AI can assist NHS staff improve the service for women attending the NHS Breast Screening Programme. "AI-assisted technology could support staff by flagging areas of a mammogram where cancer might be missed to improve early cancer detection." Yvette Cooper, Secretary of State for Health and Social Care finds out how AI is used in the EDITH trial from co-leads Professor Fiona Gilbert (left) and Professor Sian Taylor-Phillips (right). (Image: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust/Mel Yeneralski) Details of the trial will be included in screening invitation letters, along with information on how to opt out. The trial is a collaboration between the NIHR, NHS England and the UK National Screening Committee. Professor Kevin Dunbar, deputy director of public health, England, said: "The NHS Breast Screening Programme is continuing to modernise, and we are looking carefully at how technology developed using artificial intelligence could support the reading of mammograms safely and effectively. "EDITH will help build the evidence we need, while ensuring patient safety, quality and the expertise of screening professionals remain at the heart of the programme." As the trial expands, it will use AIR-SP, an AI research screening platform funded by nearly £6 million from the government. The study supports the NHS 10 Year Health Plan and the National Cancer Plan’s aims.

metadata.title: Trial to start for inmate charged with murdering Ian Huntley
metadata.contentSnippet: An inmate is due to stand trial charged with the prison murder of Soham killer Ian Huntley, who died after an attack at HMP Frankland

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Trial to start for inmate charged with murdering Ian Huntley
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: An inmate is due to stand trial charged with the prison murder of Soham killer Ian Huntley. Anthony Russell, 44, will go on trial on Monday at Newcastle Crown Court for the alleged murder of the child killer who died following an attack at HMP Frankland, near Durham. Russell is charged with a single offence of murdering the 52-year-old, who was allegedly attacked with a metal bar in a workshop at the maximum security jail on February 26. Huntley was taken to the Royal Victoria Infirmary in Newcastle, where he died on March 7. The trial is estimated to last five days. Huntley was serving a life sentence for the 2002 murders of 10-year-olds Holly Wells and Jessica Chapman. The ex-school caretaker killed the best friends after they left a family barbecue to buy sweets in Soham, Cambridgeshire, on August 4 2002. He dumped their bodies in a ditch 10 miles away. They were not found for 13 days despite a search involving hundreds of police officers. At the time, Huntley lived with Maxine Carr who was a teaching assistant at Holly and Jessica’s primary school. He denied murdering the girls but was convicted after a trial at the Old Bailey in 2003. He was jailed for life with a recommended minimum term of 40 years. Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: East of England Ambulance Service wins award for life-saving cardiac arrest video
metadata.contentSnippet: The East of England Ambulance Service has won a national award for its life-saving use of video technology.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: East of England Ambulance Service wins award for life-saving cardiac arrest video
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The East of England Ambulance Service has won a national award for its life-saving use of video technology. The service received the Digitising Patient Care Award at the HSJ Awards for its Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest Desk, which uses video calls to connect advanced paramedics with people at the scene of a cardiac arrest. This technology allows clinicians to offer real-time guidance before ambulance crews arrive, supporting CPR delivery, defibrillator use, and immediate care through a secure video link sent to a caller's smartphone. Dr Simon Walsh, medical director at the East of England Ambulance Service (EEAST), said: "Winning this award is wonderful recognition for a project that is helping save lives and supporting people during some of the most challenging moments they will ever face. "Every minute matters when someone suffers a cardiac arrest. "This technology allows our clinicians to see what is happening and support people at the scene before our crews arrive. "It helps us improve the care patients receive during the critical first minutes of a cardiac arrest and gives rescuers the confidence to act." EEAST was the first ambulance service in the UK to introduce the video system, doing so in 2025. The service has already supported 913 cardiac arrest incidents during its first 71 shifts, conducted 214 live video assessments, and recorded 421 improvements to resuscitation efforts. It has also prevented the unnecessary dispatch of 113 rapid response vehicles, 424 ambulances, and 228 managerial responses. The project was developed by EEAST and funded by the East of England Ambulance Service Charity through a £142,000 grant from NHS Charities Together, in partnership with Omaze. It has also received support from Essex & Herts Air Ambulance. The technology, powered by the GoodSAM Instant on Scene platform, is already attracting interest from other UK and international ambulance services. Dr Walsh said: "This award reflects the hard work of colleagues across EEAST, our partners at Essex & Herts Air Ambulance, and everyone who has helped develop the service, including the East of England Ambulance Service Charity and NHS Charities Together. "We are proud to see the impact it is having for patients and pleased that other ambulance services are now looking at how they can adopt similar approaches."

metadata.title: Alconbury Weald kicks off Christmas with festive market and Santa
metadata.contentSnippet: Alconbury Weald Christmas Market returns on November 28 with crafts, food, live music, Santa’s grotto and family fun, supporting the local Hardship Fund event.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Alconbury Weald kicks off Christmas with festive market and Santa
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Residents and visitors are invited to kick-start the festive season at Alconbury Weald later this month. The Alconbury Weald Christmas Market will take over the neighbourhood on Saturday, November 28, with food, crafts, live music and family fun. Natalie Leigh-Brown, senior community development lead for Alconbury Weald master developer Urban&Civic, said: "Alconbury Weald Christmas Market is a highlight of the annual events calendar, and a wonderful way to start the festive period. Locals enjoying the Christmas market. (Image: Tim George) "A huge thank you to the organisers, volunteers, Santa’s helpers—John Adams for the presents, Co-op for the wrapping paper and the Tuesday Club who wrapped the presents—the stallholders and everyone involved in creating such a special community event. "We look forward to welcoming residents, family, friends and visitors from surrounding villages and the wider area." The market, organised by the Alconbury Weald Community Association and Urban&Civic, will feature handmade crafts and gifts, toys, festive flowers, hampers and seasonal food including honey, preserves, cheese, baked goods and gin. Alconbury Weald residents enjoying the market. (Image: Tim George) Food trucks and stalls will serve jacket potatoes, hog roast and Lebanese street food, while The Watch Office Bar & Kitchen will offer Yorkshire pudding wraps, mulled wine and other festive drinks. Children from Ermine Street Church Academy will perform carols at 2.30pm, followed by live music from David Piccara between 3.30pm and 5.30pm. Alconbury Weald Christmas Market 2025. (Image: Tim George) Conor Walker will close the evening with a set of festive favourites starting at 6pm. Santa will greet children in a pop-up grotto from 2pm to 6pm, hear their Christmas wishes and hand out presents donated by John Adams, a British toy and games company based at Alconbury Weald Enterprise Campus. Santa listening to the Christmas wishes of children at the Alconbury Weald Christmas market. (Image: Tim George) Grotto places are limited and must be booked in advance. The Alconbury Weald Community Association will also run a stall offering free Christmas crafts for children and a raffle. Christmas baubles will be sold to raise money for the Hardship Fund, which helps residents facing unexpected financial difficulty or the rising cost of living.

metadata.title: £1.85m construction training centre set to open in St Neots in 2027
metadata.contentSnippet: Work has begun on a £1.85m St Neots construction training centre, offering key trade courses and opening in spring 2027 for local Cambridgeshire learners.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: £1.85m construction training centre set to open in St Neots in 2027
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Work has begun on a new £1.85 million construction training centre set to open in Cambridgeshire in spring 2027. The Eastern Education Group (EEG) will run the St Neots Construction Training Centre, offering flexible courses that meet the construction industry’s needs locally. The centre is being built on Cambridge Road at the heart of the St Neots East Expansion, on land provided by master developer Urban and Civic. Rebecca Britton (Urban and Civic), Phil Stittle (Eastern Education Group) and CPCA Mayor Paul Bristow. (Image: Eastern Education Group) Laraine Moody, executive group principal for EEG, said: "We are absolutely thrilled to have the opportunity to support people living in and around St Neots and Cambridgeshire via the creation of this state-of-the-art facility. "This centre follows on from the successful launch of our North Cambridgeshire Training Facility in Chatteris which has gone on to support the community and thousands of students and apprentices since opening in 2022. "Construction courses require specialist teaching spaces, workshops, equipment and safe working environments that cannot always be effectively delivered within traditional classroom settings." St Neots Training Centre - architect image by Dragon Heart Homes. (Image: Eastern Education Group) The centre will offer courses in carpentry and joinery, brickwork, groundwork, plumbing, and electrical installation, along with supporting subjects such as health and safety, site awareness, and sustainability. The 980-square-metre centre will include classrooms, staff offices, student breakout areas and indoor and outdoor training zones. Paul Bristow, Mayor of the Cambridgeshire & Peterborough Combined Authority (CPCA), said: "Real regional growth starts with giving local people the skills to build it. "Turning the turf on this new £1.85 million facility in St Neots is a brilliant milestone that will equip residents with practical, high-value construction trades right in the heart of a growing community." The centre is part of EEG’s new Construction Training Excellence Centre (CTEC) designation, which the group says makes it the only one of its kind in the East of England. Phil Stittle at the launch of the new construction training centre in St Neots. (Image: Eastern Education Group) Tom Sanderson, Executive Councillor for Planning at Huntingdonshire District Council, said: "The St Neots Construction Training Centre is an investment in the future of Huntingdonshire. "By developing the skills local people need to access rewarding careers in construction, we're helping to support economic growth and create opportunities for residents for years to come." The project has been funded by the Cambridgeshire & Peterborough Combined Authority, Huntingdonshire District Council, and Urban and Civic. Dragonheart Homes, Zed Pods and Lindum Group will design and build the centre, with support from Constructed Pathways. The centre is due to be completed in spring 2027.

metadata.title: Peterborough burger restaurant named top-rated on Tripadvisor with 4.9 score
metadata.contentSnippet: A Cambridgeshire burger restaurant has earned almost perfect reviews from customers, with diners praising its food and friendly service.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Peterborough burger restaurant named top-rated on Tripadvisor with 4.9 score
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Cambridgeshire burger restaurant has earned almost perfect reviews from customers, with diners praising its food and friendly service. Higgsy’s is Peterborough’s top-rated restaurant on Tripadvisor, with a 4.9 rating from hundreds of diners. The burger restaurant, at Fortune Buildings in Cowgate, is rated 4.9 out of five from 286 reviews on Tripadvisor. The website places Higgsy’s first among 469 restaurants in Peterborough. It lists the business under American, fast food and street food. Higgsy’s describes itself on its Tripadvisor listing as a smash burger company and the “home of the Redneck burger”. Its high ratings are also recorded by Restaurant Guru. The website reports a 4.9 out of five Google rating based on 341 reviews. It gives Higgsy’s a score of 4.8 out of five from more than 1,000 votes. Recent customers have praised the food and service. One Google reviewer called their meal the “BEST burger in Peterborough”, while another said everyone in their group gave the restaurant “10 out of 10”. The menu includes the Redneck Burger, other burgers, fried chicken and loaded fries. An online menu listing describes the Redneck Burger as a double smash burger with bacon, a beef frankfurter, onions and melted cheese. The restaurant offers takeaway and eating in. Its listings also mention reservations and outdoor seating. It is open from noon to 4pm and 5.30pm to 9pm from Tuesdays to Thursdays. On Fridays and Saturdays, it is listed as open from noon to 9pm. Higgsy’s is closed on Sundays and Mondays. Tripadvisor categorises the restaurant as serving American, fast food and street food, while the business presents itself as a smash burger company. The reported scores place Higgsy’s among Peterborough’s highest-rated restaurants on the review websites. Higgsy’s also trades from a layby on London Road in Yaxley, where it appealed for permission to continue operating after highway safety concerns were raised.

metadata.title: 'Legendary' cooking competition making 'explosive' return to ITV next year
metadata.contentSnippet: Hell's Kitchen is making a return to ITV next year with Gordon Ramsay coming back to help the 10 celebrity contestants.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 'Legendary' cooking competition making 'explosive' return to ITV next year
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A “legendary” cooking show is making an “explosive” return to ITV next year with a brand-new series in 2027. Hell’s Kitchen is making a comeback after its last UK series aired in 2009. The cooking competition will see Gordon Ramsay return to the kitchen to mentor the celebrity contestants. The Traitor’s star Claudia Winkleman will be taking on the role of host for the live event. Hell’s Kitchen is set to bring its “signature blend of high-stakes jeopardy and drama, intense personalities and unfiltered reality, out of the kitchen and onto our screens”. There will be a line-up of 10 celebrity contestants from social media creators and entertainment stars to sports personalities and comedians. The celebrities will be expected to deliver Michelin-standard dishes every episode. Alongside Gordon, there will be two new sous chefs and a maître D to help the celebrities with their cooking throughout the series. The live event will see 100 diners including celebrity guests, the contestants’ friends and family, and members of the public testing out the food. Claudia will be guiding the viewers and the VIP guests through the competition. The audience will be given the power to vote off the celebrity contestants who are not performing to the highest standard. Hell’s Kitchen will feature 10 episodes that are each 60 minutes long aired over two weeks and will be packed with “shocking format twists and culinary tasks”. Gordon Ramsay said: “Hell's Kitchen is returning to the UK bigger, bolder, and 100% hotter than ever before. “A brand-new restaurant, an all-star celebrity cast and culinary challenges that will push even the most confident cooks. “With live eliminations, sky-high stakes and no room for excuses, let me be very clear, every service will be a battle, and every plate will make or break their place in the competition.” Claudia Winkleman added: “I am very excited to be joining Gordon for the return of Hell's Kitchen. “It’s fast, thrilling and unpredictable live television. “I can’t wait to guide our viewers through the heat of the kitchen and am really hoping he goes easy on them, and asks for toast.” Will you be watching the new series of Hell's Kitchen? Let us know in the comments.

metadata.title: Will your Christmas present be delivered by the 'UK's worst' courier?
metadata.contentSnippet: Evri are the worst-rated couriers in 2026, according to the 'people's champions' Citizens Advice.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Will your Christmas present be delivered by the 'UK's worst' courier?
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Evri are the worst-rated couriers in 2026, according to the 'people's champions' Citizens Advice. The charity unveiled their annual league table yesterday [November 18], which rates the UK's biggest parcel delivery firms out of five. They're judged on this year's customer experiences across four categories: delivery and collection, accessibility, customer service and trust. The worst-rated courier was Evri, which picked up a 1.75 rating for delivery and collection, 2.2 for accessibility, 2.5 for customer service and 2.2 for trust, totalling an overall score of 2. The best-ranked was Royal Mail, scoring 3 for delivery and collection, 2.7 for accessibility, 2.5 for customer service and a table-high of 4.2 for trust, making a final score of 3. Amazon Logistics came second with an overall score of 2.75 after being rated 2.5 for collection and delivery, 2.5 for accessibility, 3.25 for customer service and 3.9 for trust. DPD and InPost were tied in third on 2.25 stars despite scoring slightly differently in the four tests. DPD scored 2.25 and InPost scored 2.5 for delivery and collection, for accessibility they were rated 2.3 and 2.5, for customer service 1.75 and 1 and then 3 and 2.2 for trust. InPost's 1 out of 5 rating for customer service was the lowest score in that category of all five couriers in the table. The table is part of a wider study which Citizens Advice say reveals that almost a third of parcel recipients in the past month (15 million) faced problems. They add more than a third of those (35%) saw further problems such as 'sluggish' response times or 'frustrating automated systems'. The charity warned that new accessibility requirements 'lack teeth' as they found those with accessibility needs are almost twice as likely to experience issues (45% vs 23%). Dame Clare Moriarty, chief executive of Citizens Advice, said: "Parcel deliveries are an essential part of life yet millions still bear the brunt of the dismal delivery practices normalised for too many years. "This is particularly concerning for people with accessibility needs, who are almost twice as likely to experience problems. "Consumers rarely get to choose their courier, yet they’re the ones left dealing with the consequences when things go wrong and trying to fix problems that shouldn’t be happening in the first place. "It’s clear that Ofcom’s approach isn’t working. "The regulator has the power to strengthen protections for consumers and it must. "It’s the only way to stop delivery standards flatlining and improve the market once and for all." An Evri spokesperson said: "Citizens Advice’s ranking of Evri in joint-second place for customer service out of five operators in its annual league table is testament to the significant investment we continue to make in delivering improvements Including resolving customer issues promptly and effectively. "The ranking also recognises progress in trust and accessibility. "We deliver more than a billion parcels a year and millions every day and continue to invest significantly in providing a strong and reliable service at an enormous scale. "This year alone, we have invested £32.2 million in infrastructure, technology and network capacity. "Independent data from The Despatch Company, covering 1.3 million Evri parcels, found that 99.4% were delivered within seven working days, demonstrating the strong underlying performance of our network. "We are also continuing to make it easier for customers to get support when they need it, while investing in accessibility and greater choice. "More than 200,000 accessibility preferences have now been set by customers, which is more than double the number a year ago, alongside improvements to accessibility information across our ParcelShop and locker network. "Citizen's Advice has also awarded Evri the highest accessibility policy score of all operators assessed which recognises the significant work and investment we continue to make to improve the customer experience. "Overall, we know there is more to do and will continue listening to customers and acting on their feedback. "Our focus remains on continuously improving customer experiences and making practical changes that deliver better outcomes for everyone." A Royal Mail spokesperson said: "We’re pleased to lead Citizens Advice’s Parcels League Table again this year by ranking first for customer trust and for delivery and collection. "As the UK’s postal service, we want everyone to be able to send and receive parcels easily. "We’ve been working to make our services more accessible and ranked first in the new Accessibility League Table but we know there’s more to do, both at Royal Mail and across the industry. "With Christmas approaching, customers are counting on us to get their cards and presents there on time. "We’ve been preparing since January and we’re ready for the extra mail. "In each of the past two years more than 99% of items posted by our last recommended posting dates arrived in time for Christmas and we intend to deliver the same again this year." Amazon, DPD and InPost were all contacted for comment. Ofcom have been contacted for comment.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A new publican is being sought to take the reins of a "characterful" and much-loved pub in a Cambridgeshire town. The White Horse, in Eaton Socon, St Neots, is looking for an experienced operator who can take on the "charming listed building". Stonegate describes the premises as "farm more than a traditional pub operation". It boasts a "substantial commercial kitchen", "versatile internal trading spaces",  "extensive beer garden" and an outdoor bar. The pub also has a bandstand for live entertainment, customer parking and potential letting opportunities. It presents "multiple opportunities to develop a thriving hospital business with several revenue streams". The pub previously operated a highly successful carvery and benefits from a "loyal local following". It also benefits from a roadside location between the A1 and A428, which provides "strong passing trade and access to a growing customer base". Also included is "generous" private accommodation with five bedrooms, two bathrooms, a lounge, kitchen, office and storage room. Katy Jones, regional manager at Stonegate Group, said: “The White Horse is a beautiful, characterful building in a fantastic location with huge potential for the right operator. "We're looking for an experienced publican, ideally with a strong food background, who can build on the pub's excellent reputation. "With its extensive trading space, established food credentials, outdoor facilities and additional income opportunities, The White Horse offers a genuine chance to create a successful multi-faceted hospitality business." Stonegate said it hopes to find an operator who can "build on the pub's strong foundations and help secure its future as a valued community hub for years to come." summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Staff at a doctor's surgery in Cambridgeshire have been left "deeply saddened" after its automatic front doors were "vandalised". The Charles Hicks Centre, in Huntingdon, revealed staff had arrived to discover the doors, which were installed to improve disabled access, had been damaged. The wiring to the doors was "cut" just days after they were installed, in what the surgery has described as a "senseless act". Practice manage, Lisa Harrison, said the incident likely occurred between 6.30pm on Thursday (November 19) and 7.30am the next day. The surgery described the incident as a "senseless act" (Image: The Hicks Group Practice) She added: "The doors have been badly scratched and the wiring has been cut, leaving the automatic entrance completely unusable. "This is a senseless act that directly impacts our most vulnerable patients and diverts vital funds away from patient care to cover the cost of urgent repairs. "We have reported the incident to Cambridgeshire Constabulary and are working closely with engineers to get the doors fixed as quickly as possible. "In the meantime, our team is on hand to help anyone entering the building. "We urge anyone who saw or heard anything suspicious around Ermine Street last night to contact the police." Cambridgeshire Police has been contacted for further information. Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

If that wasn't enough, the restaurant received the Trip Advisor Traveller's Choice award in September last year. Reviews from millions of Trip Advisor travellers placed the award-winning venue in the top 10 per cent of restaurants worldwide. Manager Abul Chowdhury told The Hunts Post the restaurant continues to "attract large numbers of customers" in spite of the rising cost of living. One visitor said: "Can honestly say it’s probably the best Indian meal I have ever eaten, flavours were fantastic and portion sizes were spot on. "The staff were very friendly. Will definitely be returning and would fully recommend." Another added: "Warm welcome, lovely food, quality ingredients, tasted flavoursome. Very courteous staff, how customer service should be." metadata.title: The best woodland walks in Cambridgeshire to discover this autumn
metadata.contentSnippet: From ancient woodlands and National Trust estates to wildlife-rich nature reserves, Cambridgeshire offers far more woodland scenery than many people realise.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: The best woodland walks in Cambridgeshire to discover this autumn
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: From ancient woodlands and National Trust estates to wildlife-rich nature reserves, Cambridgeshire offers far more woodland scenery than many people realise. Showcasing some of the county's most attractive forest and woodland walks, here are six beauty spots to discover this autumn. While best known for its wetlands, Wicken Fen also contains areas of woodland and scrub that create a wonderfully varied walking experience. The reserve's network of paths passes through reedbeds, grassland and developing woodland, offering visitors the chance to spot everything from dragonflies and marsh harriers to grazing Konik ponies. The ever-changing landscape and huge skies make every walk feel different, whatever the season. One of the county's most important ancient woodlands, Monk's Wood is a haven for wildlife and a favourite among walkers seeking tranquillity. The reserve's oak and ash trees line peaceful trails that weave through centuries-old woodland. In spring, woodland flowers brighten the forest floor, while birdwatchers can spot woodpeckers, nuthatches and other species. The largest country estate in Cambridgeshire offers far more than historic architecture. Its extensive parkland includes pockets of mature woodland, tree-lined avenues and scenic walking routes stretching across the estate. Visitors can wander beneath ancient trees before emerging into open countryside with far-reaching views. Managed by the National Trust, it combines woodland beauty with some of the county's most impressive landscapes. Famous for its gardens, Anglesey Abbey also boasts beautiful woodland walks that are particularly spectacular during autumn. Shaded paths wind through mature trees and carefully designed landscapes, creating a peaceful retreat from nearby Cambridge. Seasonal colour is a major draw, while the estate's varied habitats support a wide range of birds and other wildlife. It is one of the most picturesque places for a gentle woodland stroll in the county. Covering more than 170 acres, Hinchingbrooke Country Park combines mature woodland with lakes, meadows and open countryside. Well-maintained trails guide visitors through shady woodland areas rich in birdlife and seasonal wildflowers. The park's accessibility and variety of routes make it popular with families, dog walkers and runners alike, while its peaceful setting provides a welcome escape from nearby Huntingdon. One of Cambridgeshire's most diverse nature reserves, Paxton Pits features woodland trails alongside lakes, meadows and wetlands. The reserve is particularly popular with wildlife enthusiasts thanks to its rich birdlife and varied habitats. Visitors can enjoy peaceful woodland walks before exploring the waterside paths and observation points. At Paxton Pits, the Heron Trail and Meadow Trail offer opportunities to spot wildlife around the reserve's lakes as the seasons change. Have you got a story you want to share? summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Love exploring green spaces and fancy a nice walk? Then this much-loved country park in Cambridgeshire is for you. Described a "hidden gem" by visitors, Hinchingbrooke Country Park offers the perfect haven for those looking for a peaceful escape. Tucked away just outside of Huntingdon, the estate spans 150-acres, combining open grassland, mature woodland and lakes. It's a great spot for walkers, nature lovers and young families alike. Visitors can enjoy walking trails through wildflower meadows and woodlands or enjoy the mix of play areas, a café and muddy paths. Perhaps unsurprisingly, Hinchingbrooke County Park has held the Green Flag Award since 2018. Recognising the best parks and green spaces internationally, the scheme provides the high standards against which sites are measured. Whether you've explored the park or its your first time visiting, there is something for everyone. Hinchingbrooke Country Park remains a favourite for dog walkers, nature spotters and anyone looking to enjoy the outdoors in a peaceful, natural setting. It boasts a wealth of wildlife, including sightings of all three species of British woodpecker along with the nuthatch and marsh tit. Sharing what to expect, Huntingdonshire District Council says: "Whether you are walking the dog, exploring with your children, having a picnic or enjoying tea and cakes or ice creams from the café, we are sure you will enjoy your visit." Unsurprisingly, then, the park has received rave reviews on Trip Advisor, averaging 4.4 out of 5 based on more than 200 reviews. One visitor said: "Beautiful hidden gem. It is perfect for a pleasant stroll, there is plenty of parking and even a small café for a refreshment after." Another added: "Nice, big, open expanse of a park, with many easy walks. Lots of space for families to enjoy and for dog walkers to exercise their best buddies." What's your favourite walk in Cambridgeshire? Let us know in the comments.
