metadata.title: 9 hidden gems in Cambridgeshire you have to visit at least once
metadata.contentSnippet: Cambridgeshire is packed with hidden gems that rarely make the county's tourism brochures.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 9 hidden gems in Cambridgeshire you have to visit at least once
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Cambridgeshire is packed with hidden gems that rarely make the county's tourism brochures. From ancient wetlands and secret nature reserves to forgotten archaeological sites and historic country estates, here are nine lesser-known attractions to visit. Often described as a hidden gem, Wicken Fen is the National Trust's oldest nature reserve and one of Europe's most important wetlands. Visitors can explore boardwalks winding through reedbeds, marshes and wildflower meadows while spotting dragonflies, rare birds and grazing Highland cattle. The reserve offers a glimpse into the ancient Fenland landscape that once dominated the region, making it an excellent destination for walkers, families and wildlife enthusiasts. Hidden away between Peterborough and Huntingdon, Holme Fen feels remarkably wild and remote. The reserve is home to the famous Holme Post, marking Britain's lowest land point at around 2.75 metres below sea level. Visitors can explore peaceful woodland trails, wetlands and bird hides while discovering a fascinating story of how drainage transformed the Fens. One of Britain's last remaining washlands, Nene Washes offers spectacular wildlife viewing throughout the year. Winter floods attract thousands of migratory birds, while spring and summer bring breeding cranes, godwits and marsh harriers. Birdwatchers rate it among the county's finest locations, yet it remains surprisingly under the radar with many local visitors. Covering hundreds of acres beside the River Nene, the park combines lakes, woodland, meadows and cycle routes. Families can enjoy water sports, miniature railways, walking trails and abundant wildlife. Created from former gravel workings, Paxton Pits has become one of Cambridgeshire's most important wildlife sites. Its lakes, reedbeds and woodland attract kingfishers, otters and hundreds of bird species throughout the year. Well-maintained trails and viewing hides make it accessible for families, photographers and nature lovers alike. Many visitors compare the reserve favourably with much larger national wildlife attractions while enjoying a quieter atmosphere. One of the most significant Bronze Age archaeological sites in Britain, Flag Fen remains surprisingly little known outside the region. The attraction centres on a 3,500-year-old causeway preserved beneath the peat and waterlogged soils of the Fens. Interactive exhibits, reconstructed roundhouses and fascinating artefacts help bring prehistoric Cambridgeshire to life. One of the largest habitat restoration projects in the country, Ouse Fen offers expansive wetland scenery and exceptional birdwatching opportunities. Visitors can enjoy peaceful walking trails through reedbeds and lakes while looking out for cranes, bitterns and marsh harriers. The sheer scale of the reserve creates an extraordinary sense of isolation, despite being only a short distance from Ely and nearby villages. Tucked inside Huntingdon's former grammar school, the Cromwell Museum tells the story of Oliver Cromwell and the English Civil War through a collection of nationally important artefacts. Despite its historical significance, it remains relatively overlooked compared with larger museums in Cambridge. Visitors can examine weapons, portraits and personal items linked to one of Britain's most influential and controversial historical figures. Located just outside Peterborough, Sacrewell blends history, countryside and family-friendly attractions. Highlights include a restored 19th-century watermill, rare farm animals, woodland walks and seasonal events. The setting offers a gentler and quieter alternative to larger commercial attractions while still providing plenty to keep children entertained. Its combination of heritage and outdoor space makes it particularly appealing for multi-generational visits. Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: St Neots academy chosen for international reading partnership with Morocco school
metadata.contentSnippet: Longsands Academy in St Neots joins 25 UK schools in British Council reading scheme, partnering with Morocco’s Tazemourt Middle School to boost literacy.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: St Neots academy chosen for international reading partnership with Morocco school
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A St Neots academy has been chosen as one of 25 UK schools taking part in an international reading programme. Longsands Academy is one of 25 UK schools in the Reading for Pleasure scheme, which builds international links and promotes reading, writing and oracy. The British Council runs the programme with support from the National Literacy Trust, pairing Longsands Academy with Tazemourt Middle School in Souss-Massa, Morocco. Michael Cox, vice principal at Longsands Academy, said: "This is a really exciting partnership and I feel incredibly privileged to visit Morocco and to witness first hand what this link up will create for our students. Longsands pupils writing letters to students in Morocco. (Image: Astrea Academy Trust) "I was honoured to hand over written letters from our students at Longsands and meet our partner teacher at Tazemourt Middle School, we have so many brilliant ideas to work on together. "By connecting our schools, we will enhance reading, writing and oracy across Longsands, giving students valuable lifelong skills and international friendships." The project is already under way, with Mr Cox meeting Moroccan English teacher Asma Jegni during a recent visit where he delivered written letters from Longsands students. Umara Qureshi, principal at Longsands Academy, said: "I am so proud to see Longsands Academy represented on the international stage through the British Council UK-Morocco Reading for Pleasure Schools Partnership Programme. "A huge thank you to Michael for his commitment to expanding opportunities for our students and bringing back innovative ideas that will further strengthen our reading culture." Vice Principal Michael Cox (right) with Asma Jegni (left), an English teacher from their partner school in Morocco. (Image: Astrea Academy Trust) The Reading for Pleasure project is supported by the National Literacy Trust and forms part of the British Council's work to encourage international understanding and collaboration between schools.

th
 
May 2026 as a correct record. 
 
236.Nomination For Freedom of the Town. 
The nomination is for retired Councillor Mrs Pat Taylor. 
As you know Pat has been a long-standing member of council, serving twice as our Mayor once for a 
three-year term and then another for a two-year term and held the position of Deputy Mayor on 
several occasions. Mrs Taylor served from 14
th
 September 1989 and is well known for her work as a 
teacher at the Ailwyn as an English teacher. Proposed by Cllr A Costello and seconded by Cllr S 
Corney, Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION (the member did not agree with 
these types of awards) for the Freedom of the Town to be awarded to Mrs Pat Taylor. 
 
237. Planning Applications for Consideration 
1.1 26/00761/FUL Conversion of two flats into three-bedroom house – 39 Great Whyte Ramsey. 
Proposed by Cllr S Corney and Cllr S Fice. Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the 
District Council to APPROVE the application. Members agreed it was the best for the property to turn 
back into a family home, has a driveway so no extra pressure on parking. 
 
1.2 26/00640/FUL Permanent use of land for 2 static caravans and 1 touring caravan for Gypsy and 
Traveller purposes.  Erection of dayroom building and associated works – Land on South Side of 
Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights. There was a large debate about this planning application and 
members want it noted that businesses are being run from down Middle Drove which is not permitted. 
The information given at the Development Management Committee on 16
th
 March about the distance 
to the local schools and shops was incorrect and also at that meeting it was said it had a good bus 
route- the bus has to go into Peterborough first so to get to Ramsey from Ramsey Heights via bus is a 
two-hour journey. Cllr V Fendley informed the members that the Neighbourhood Plan consultant has 
added an appendix to the document which outlines the restriction zones that impact the Nature 
Reserve and human sewage going into the waterways. The .gov site  
www.gov.uk/government/publications/planning-policy-for-traveller-sites/planning-policy-for-traveller-sites 
policy C was read out by the Clerk and Cllr A Costello read out policy E, Cllr S Fice also read out other 
sections from the document in particular point 13 flood risk which the site is 3A. Cllr J Clarke spoke 
about septic tanks are no longer permitted and need to be referred to as ‘klargester septic tanks’ 
Cllr V Fendley informed members that the two Freedom of Information requests to Huntingdonshire 
District Council and Cambridgeshire Police had not been responded to, the Clerk fed back that they 
had been chased up. It was noted that the Environment agency stated that the Internal Drainage 
Board had not made comment and Cllr J Clarke said he would be attending a meeting and would give 
feedback on this and ask for comment. Proposed by Cllr A Costello and seconded by Cllr S Fice, 
Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to REFUSE the application. 
There were no resident objections on the planning portal as they cannot redact their addresses and 

fear reprisals, but the following resident comments had been received by the Clerk and as previously 
been agreed with Huntingdonshire District Council they would be submitted by Ramsey Town 
Council.  
 
1) The landscape on both middle drove and harpers drove has changed dramatically over the last 7 yo 8 
years,  the countryside has been eroded away by concrete and static caravans and large chalet type buildings 
being placed  onto the fields that was once agricultural land, and the wildlife on the droves are being left with no 
habitat,  the view of the countryside has also changed over the last 7 to 8  years. 
 
2) sightings of Great crested newts have now been spotted on harpers drove very close to Uggmere Court Road 
and adjoining fields with middle drove,  we have now sent pictures to the great crested newts society and we are 
awaiting a site visit to extend the zone from walton fen nature reserve to Uggmere Court Road to protect them. 
 
3) The existing settled community on middle drove and school drove and harpers drove are not in balance with 
the traveller community and the existing settled community are now feeling that they have lost their own 
community and at times overwhelmed by the the large and ever growing traveller community that has already 
moved on to middle drove and harpers drove without any permission . 
 
4) The settled community are scared to challenge or voice their concerns to any anti social behaviour from the 
traveller community,  unable to call the police due to reprisals from the large community several residents have 
had property destroyed by the traveller community as a warning.  
 
5) Middle drove and harpers drove are now know as the crime capital of Ramsey,  this has made residents feel 
completely uneasy and ashamed to live in the ramsey heights area. 
 
6) The traveller community do not allow dogs into their homes as family pets , so they are housed outside in 
kennels, which leads to barking 24/7 , . 
 
7) The two community's are not compatible in such close proximity to each other its like two different world's 
have  collided.  
 
8) The volume of traffic that is now using the drove is causing the repairs to the drove to be carried out several 
times a year now , and the dust is causing residents to keep windows and doors closed.  
 
Below are just some of the anti social behaviours we have to contend with on a daily basis.  
 
 
1,tow trucks crashing over speed ramps day and night no consideration for residents.  
 
2, tree cutting services dropping waste from the backs of trucks , and left on the drove. 
 
3, scrap vehicles being transported down the gravel drove and dropping parts onto the drove. 
 
4, Off road motorbikes being driven at high speeds during the day and late into the evenings by children and 
adults.  
 
5, The burning of toxic materials during the day which means residents are unable to have washing out and have 
to have windows closed even during the hot summer months.  
 
6, speeding vehicles driven with no tax or insurance on the drove. 
 
7, The severe crime levels that now affect both droves , , 
 cannabis factory's being set up continuously, stolen vehicles,  stolen trailers,  stolen caravans,  stolen 
commercial vehicles, stolen tools,  
Traveller disputes taking place on the drove burnt-out tow trucks. 
 
8, The cutting into water supply and electricity.  
 
This is an honest opinion of how residents feel on middle drove and school drove and harpers drove and 
surrounding  

 
1.3 26/00642/FUL Permanent use for 1 mobile home and 1 touring caravan.  Erection of dayroom 
building and associated works – Land on South Side of Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights. After a long 
discussion which included noting the site was already there with temporary planning permission but 
now wanted permanent status and adding an extra dayroom which members commented was a 
bungalow minus a named bedroom, Proposed by Cllr A Costello and seconded by Cllr C Maskell, 
Ramsey Town Council voted 9 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION for the District Council to REFUSE the 
application. The comments previously submitted by the residents on 1.2 will also be submitted along 
with the Town Councils comments on overdevelopment of Gypsy / Traveller sites, no amenities, flood 
risk 3A, criminal activity. 
 
1.4 26/00752/FUL Change of use of land to mixed use Equestrian and Gypsy/Traveller site 
and the erection of a shared dayroom (retrospective) – Land Northwest of Two Acres, 
Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr A 
Costello, Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLEY for the District Council to 
REFUSE the application. It is overdevelopment in the countryside, and flood risk 3A. The 
comments from residents on 1.2 would also be submitted. 
1.5 26/00920/TREE Tree application – Tesco Stores Ltd, Neil Way, Ramsey. Proposed by Cllr S 
Corney and seconded by Cllr L Knight, Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the 
District Council to APPROVE the application and take the advice from the HDC Tree Officer. 
 
1.6 26/00481/HHFUL Single storey side extension and new driveway – 39 Station Road, Ramsey. 
Proposed by Cllr S Fice and seconded by Cllr L Knight, Ramsey Town Council vote 
UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the application. Members noted the change 
of angle with the driveway and the updated comments from Cambridgeshire Highways. 
 
238. Planning Other Business: 
1- To be advised that Additional Sites Allocations for the Local Plan to 2046 will be 
available to view and comment between 13 May and 10 July. noted 
2- HDC have publicised that both The Ramsey Communities (Regulation 16) 
Neighbourhood Plan and The Giddings, Winwick and Hamerton (Reg 16) 
Neighbourhood Plan will be available to view and comment on between 11 May and 
23 June. noted 
3- Update on Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan. Cllr V Fendley informed 
members that Huntingdonshire District Council had put forward two potential 
independent inspectors and we had been advised to ask for others and another name 
had been put forward. The NHP consultant would now do research and bring to the 
meeting for members to choose their preferred inspector. Cllr V Fendley informed the 
members that they look at areas of difference between the Ramsey Communities 
Neighbourhood Plan and the District Council Local Plan and they are the field between 
Ramsey Rural Museum and the 1940s Camp and the piece of land which David 
Wilson Homes was trying to build on between Ramsey and Bury. noted 
4- Abbey College Local Highways Initiative Bid (LHI). Members had tabled a plan of the 
speed cushions proposed in the Abbey College LHI bid and had been asked to 
comment on their positioning. After a detailed discussion and Cllr J Bufton spoke to 
members on his position of wanting no speed calming on Hollow Lane and felt the 
problems were caused by the lack of awareness of students themselves and that 
residents should not have to have speed cushions on the Lane all year round. Cllr J 
Clarke also asked that a comment went back to ensure the bus companies who 
transport the children were consulted for comment. Proposed by Cllr S Fice and 
seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 7 FOR and 3 ABSTENTIONS 
for the following comments to be fed back to Abbey College Road Safety Group. 
Ramsey Town Council are pleased that speed cushion no.6 on the plan had been 
removed. They would ask the group to remove speed cushion 5 on the plan as they 
felt it would push the vehicles parking further up Hollow Lane and they would like the 
group to consider speed cushion 4 to be moved away from the junction and moved 

west. Ramsey Town Council would like the group to consult with the bus companies 
that transport the students for comment. 
 
 
239. Meeting Dates 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council will take place on 11th June 2026 at 7pm.

held at 7pm on Thursday 25 June 2026  at  
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey 
 
 
Present:  Councillors: I Axelsen, M Clarke, S Corney (Dep Mayor), V Fendley (Mayor),S

250. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved. 
Having  been proposed  by Cllr S Corney and seconded  by Cllr P  Rose, Council voted 
unanimously to APPROVE the Minutes of the meeting of 11th June 2026 as a correct record. 
 
251. Planning Applications for Consideration 
1.1 26/00433/FUL Change  of  use  of  stable  block  to  utility  block/day  room – Land  West  of 
Goodlife Cottage, Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by 
Cllr R Terrill. Ramsey Town Council voted unanimously to recommend that the District Council 
REFUSE the application and would be commenting as per the comments provided by the Town 
Council’s Planning Consultant. 
1.2 26/00949/S73 Variation of condition 2 (approved plans) of 24/01721/HHFUL – Heathfield, 
Benwick Road, Ramsey Forty Foot. Having been proposed by Cllr Rose and Seconded by Cllr 
Corney Council  voted unanimously to  recommend  that  the  District  Council APPROVE the 
application, there had been no neighbouring objections. 
1.3 26/01053/TELDET Installation  of  1  power  generator,  1  equipment  cabinet  and  ancillary 
development  thereto – Ramsey  Water  Tower,  The  Malting,  Ramsey.    Having  considered 
comments submitted by Cllr A Austin councillors agreed to support the installation. Having been 
proposed  by  Cllr S Fice  and  seconded  by  Cllr L Webster,  council voted unanimously to 
recommend APPROVAL. 
 
252. Planning Other Business 
Councillors noted an update from Cllr Fendley on the Shop in a Box project.  Cllr Fendley had 
been informed that details of the proposed project had been sent to the Town Council ahead 
of a planning application for the work.  The proposal would be for a shepherd hut design due 
to the  weight  limit  on the  road,  all  huts  would  have electricity, but  no  running  water  and  Cllr 
Axelson  raised  concern  over  the  disposal  of any wastewater.  HDC had  tendered for  a

Present:  Councillors: I Axelsen, M Clarke, S Corney (Dep Mayor), V Fendley (Mayor),S Fice, L Knight, C Maskell, P Rose, R Terrill and L Webster. In attendance: Mrs A Jerrom, Deputy Town Clerk
247. Apologies for Absence. Cllrs A Austin, J Bufton, J Clarke and E Welsh.

250. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved. Having  been proposed  by Cllr S Corney and seconded  by Cllr P  Rose, Council voted unanimously to APPROVE the Minutes of the meeting of 11th June 2026 as a correct record.

251. Planning Applications for Consideration 1.1 26/00433/FUL Change  of  use  of  stable  block  to  utility  block/day  room – Land  West  of Goodlife Cottage, Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights. RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL 
 
You are hereby summoned to attend a meeting of Ramsey Town Council to be held in The Lavender Room, 
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey on Thursday 23 July 2026 at 7.00pm, when the following 
items of business will be transacted: - 
 
 
Please ensure all mobile phones are switched off or turned to silent during the meeting. 
 
A G E N D A  
   APOLOGIES FOR ABSENCE 
 
1. DECLARATIONS OF INTEREST 
To receive declarations from Members as to disclosable pecuniary and other interests and the nature of 
those interests in relation to any agenda item. 
   
2. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

3. MINUTES 
To approve as a correct record, the Minutes of the meeting of the Council held on 9th July 2026 – 
attached. 
 
 
4. PLANNING 
1.1 26/01172/HHFUL – Two storey rear extension, single storey extension, replace garage flat roof with 
mono pitch roof alterations – 11 Windsor Drive, Ramsey Forty Foot. 
 
 
Would Cllrs please make time to look at the planning items on the District Council’s website 
before the meeting by accessing the HDC planning portal.  
  
  
5. MEETING DATES 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council will take place at 7pm on 13th August 2026.  
 
 
 Lisa Renfree                           17th July 2026 
     
      Town Clerk 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

MINUTES OF RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL MEETING 
held at 7pm on Thursday 9 July 2026 at  
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey 
 
 
Present:  Councillors: A Austin, I Axelsen, J Bufton, J Clarke, M Clarke, S Corney (Dep Mayor), V Fendley 
(Mayor), S Fice, C Maskell, R Terrill and L Webster. 
In attendance: Mrs L Renfree, Town Clerk  
 
254. Apologies for Absence. 
Cllrs J Aubin, J Clarke, L Knight, P Rose, and E Welsh. The Clerk informed members that Cllr Rebecca Cope 
had sent in by email her resignation that afternoon. 
 
Cllr V Fendley welcomed Cllr L Webster to her first Full Council meeting. 
  
255.To Receive Declarations of Interest. 
There were no Declarations of Interest. 
 
256. Public Participation. 
There were two members of the public present. 
 
257. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved. 
Having  been proposed  by  Cllr  S  Corney  and  seconded  by  Cllr  M  Clarke,  Council voted 10  FOR and 1 
ABSTENTION for the Minutes of the meeting of 25th June 2026 as a correct record. 
 
258.  District  Councillor  Update. Cllrs  H  Tobias,  K  Maheshwari  and  R  Coogan  had  been  invited  to  address 
Town Council Members.  
Cllr K Maheshwari had put in his apologies, but no apologies were received by Cllr H Tobias or Cllr R Coogan. 
The Clerk read an email report from K Maheshwari  
‘Although I am unable to attend this meeting, I would like to provide a brief update. 
I continue to hold regular meetings with constituents and remain accessible by email and through my social 
media channels, ensuring residents can contact me whenever they need assistance. 
Where issues raised by residents require the involvement of Ramsey Town Council, I copy the Town Council 
into the relevant correspondence so that matters can be dealt with collaboratively. 
Since the last Town Council meeting, no issues have been referred to me by Ramsey Town Council that require 
an update. However, I remain available to assist the Town Council, fellow councillors and residents whenever 
support is needed. Please do not hesitate to contact me if there are any district council matters on which I can 
help. 
Thank you, and I look forward to continuing to work together for the benefit of Ramsey and the surrounding 
communities. 
Thanks 
Kind regards 
Cllr Karan Maheshwari 
Council members were very disappointed that there was no District Councillor present to represent 
Huntingdonshire District Council and asked the Clerk to raise this with them. Further feedback was that in Cllr 
Maheshwari report he stated he had not been asked to do any work on behalf of Ramsey Town Council, Cllr S 
Corney reminded members that he been asked to speak to Huntingdonshire District Council about the land at 
the back of the Doctors Surgery on Mews Close, and that Cllr S Corney had spoken to him at length after the 
meeting about the project and how to approach the Officers. It was also commented that Cllr K Maheshwari had 
been promoting all local events and had not promoted the 4
th
 July Party in the Park a Town Council event. The 
Clerk had been asked to correspond with the three District Councillors for clarity on these issues and to gain 
commitment for future meetings. 
 
259. Planning Applications for Consideration 
1.1  26/01152/OUT Proposed  outline  application  for  development  of  up  to  19  residential  dwellings  with  matters 
committed  to  access.  Hankins  Garage  46  Whytefield Road.  Ramsey  PE26  1AH.After  a  lengthy  discussion 
Proposed by Cllr L Webster and seconded by Cllr S Fice Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the 
District Council to APPROVE the outline plan but wanted the following comments to be noted for further plans.  
Ramsey Town Council members suggested the following: 
• having a lesser number of houses on the plot and increase the number of car parking spaces.  
• To have allocated visitor parking to take pressure away from Whytefield Road.  
• Have concerns where the flow of the attenuation pond would flow to 

• Suggest bungalow housing maybe preferable and take pressure away from parking spaces required. 
• There  is  a  strip  of  land  that  goes  from  the  site  to  Blenheim  Road  and  even  though  it  is  outside  of  the 
application boundary was assurance this would not be used for traffic. 
• Council felt the application should make S106 and CIL contribution. 
260. Planning Other Business 
a)  TRO – pedestrianisation – The  Clerk  informed members  that  the  TRO  was  now  being  looked  at  by 
Cambridgeshire Highways and work should start in September. 
b) Street Naming to be noted. Static Caravan, Land Southeast of True Briton, Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights to 
be known as Hare’s Place - Noted 
c) Cllr V Fendley informed members that Huntingdonshire District Council had appointed the Independent 
Assessor for the Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan and they had started to ask questions which 
Anthony Northcote the Planning Advisor was answering. Cllr J Clarke asked if the answers would go through 
Ramsey Town Council, Cllr V Fendley reminded Members that the Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan 
Steering Group would be overseeing the process. 
 
261. Finance Items. 
a) Financial Summary – Cashbook to 30/06/2026 which was tabled. Noted. 
b) Expenditure Transactions to be approved. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr A Austin Ramsey 
Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the expenditure transactions to be APPROVED 
c) The Clerk informed Members that the invoice had been received from Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust for 
£3750. Cllr I Axelsen declared a non-pecuniary interest in this item as Chair of Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust 
and would not vote. After a discussion on how the youth provision was improving it was Proposed by Cllr S Fice 
and seconded by Cllr M Clarke Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION for the Clerk to pay 
the invoice. 
 
262. Working Party Recommendations. 
Cemetery Working Party 
For Council to agree to explore the option of having green burials in the Cemetery Extension, working in 
partnership with Muchwood. Cllr M Clarke informed members of the discussion that had taken place with 
herself, Cllr A Costello, Chris from Muchwood and the Clerk. The recommendation was for the Cemetery 
Working Party to look further into partnership working with Muchwood for a Green Burial Site on the extension 
section of the Wood Lane Cemetery. Proposed by Cllr M Clarke and seconded by Cllr A Costello, Ramsey 
Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the Cemetery Working Party to continue to explore the opportunity for 
partnership working and feed back to Full Council. 
Cllr M Clarke handed over to Cllr A Costello for an update on the Mortuary Chapel. 
Cllr A Costello informed members that she had met with Nick Armour from Huntingdonshire District Council 
Conservation Team. The most urgent part of the restoration was to remove the glass of the contagion windows. 
Cllr A Costello had been contacting glass companies but there was a resistance to do the work. Cllr S Corney 
had passed on a contact who is prepared to do the work and is a Carpenter and Glazier, within the previously 
agreed limit and using the money donated by the Friends of the Mortuary Chapel the Clerk had engaged Sean 
Bellamy at a cost of £600 to remove the glass. 
Nick Armour also said to Councillor A Costello that with the plans the Town Council had for the site we should 
explore using Huntingdonshire District Council CIL funds. 
 
263. Abuse towards Council Employees and Ramsey Town Councillors. 
Ramsey Town Council Members had been made aware of a known individual who had been targeting the Town 
Clerk with verbal abuse, this person had also been abusive toward other Councillors and members of the 
public. This is now being investigated by Cambridgeshire Police. Cllr A Austin reminded the Clerk that if she 
requires immediate support to call the Emergency What’s App and a member would come to support. The Clerk 
along with council staff have access to a panic button as part of the Lone Working Policy. It was agreed the 
situation would be monitored. 
 
264. TOWN MAYOR’S AND CLERK’S CORRESPONDENCE: 
a) Cllr H Tobias email to the Clerk and response – Council to consider if any further comments are required – 
letter previously circulated. The Clerk had previously circulated an email and response that she had received 
from Huntingdonshire District Councillor for Ramsey Cllr Howard Tobias. The Clerk was instructed to write a 
further letter to Cllr H Tobais explaining the legislation that Town Council follow and cannot raise funds for other 
public bodies, to advise Cllr H Tobias to have a meeting with the Police and Crime Commissioner Daryl Preston 
who can influence where funds are spent on Policing. The Clerk was also asked to reiterate that the offer to use 
the facilities of Ramsey Town Council, the library was still available and to explore the use of the Ramsey Fire 
Station. 

 
b) Parking on Abbey Road. The Clerk informed Council that residents of Abbey Road had expressed concern 
over the parking plans at Abbey College. They were currently suffering from excess parking outside their 
properties and wanted to know what they could do. The Clerk had spoken with them and given advice. Cllr J 
Clarke did not think the road was private as the council had adopted the road from Hollow Lane to the Last 
house. Cllr J Bufton thought the bus turn around and the road to the school could be private and belong to the 
school. Cllr J Bufton suggested we note the residents’ comments but knowing that there will always have 
parking in Abbey Road because the school shut the gates for a short period of time each day.  
 
265. Freedom of Information Request from Ramsey Town Council 
FOI received from Huntingdonshire District Council this had previously been circulated to members and whilst 
they were disappointed in the response no further action would take place at this time. 
FOI Cambridgeshire Police – a response had now been received and would be circulated to members. 
 
266. ATTENDANCES AT MEETINGS AND ORGANISATIONS: 
• Cllr V Fendley and Cllr R Terrill had attended the Bishop of Ely’s Garden Party, a lovely event and was 
able to meet many other dignitaries from Cambridgeshire. 
• The Clerk fed back from the 4
th
 July event, saying the feedback was, more please, and that ideas had 
been given for future event. 
• Cllr V Fendley fed back on a meeting she had attended online with Michelle Sacks CEO of 
Huntingdonshire District Council. Elections for the shadow authorities will take place next May. There is 
not an appeal process but if the authority had a strong case it could go to judicial review, or they could 
ask for some boundary amendments. The transition will still happen in May 2028. Regarding selling of 
Community Assets, they must still follow process and not sell the assets cheaply as it could impact the 
new Unitary. CIL can still be awarded even if it is for a future project and the funds can be ring-fenced. 
• Cllr C Maskell fed back about how well the Bands on the Green had been, each week had seen more 
than one hundred plus residents of all ages. 
• Cllr S Fice had attended the Ramsey St Mary’s PCC Strawberry Tea, which helps raise funds towards 
keeping the church open. 
• Cllr V Fendley informed members that the Project team had appointed Retail Revival to put together two 
business plans; one would be if Council was operating and one if it was operated through a social 
enterprise. 
•  Cllr V Fendley and the Clerk attended the Ramsey Junior School Eco Day and gave away previously 
prepared envelopes of wildflower seed by the Council staff team for the children to spread in their 
gardens. 
• Cllr V Fendley thanked the Council for supporting Once Upon a Time in Fenland which took place at 
Ramsey Rural Museum. Children from Ramsey Junior school and Ashbeach school attended and with 
the extra showing funded by Ramsey Town Council other groups including the Brownies attended 
meaning over 200 children had seen the show. 
           Cllr C Maskell left the meeting at 8:20pm 
 
• Cllr V Fendley had also attended the Ramsey Rotary handover and informed members that Chris Wick 
would be the President for this year. 
• Cllr V Fendley attended the Army Cadet showcase in Waterbeach, supporting the Ramsey Cadets and 
was disappointed no other Mayor’s supported their groups. 
• Cllr V Fendley attended AGE UK launch of Befriending Service in care homes. 60% of people in care 
homes do not receive visitors. This was held at Magnolia Park. 
• Cllr R Terrill and Cllr V Fendley attended the online Police meeting with Inspector Colin Norden. When 
challenged about the lack of PCSO’s for Ramsey they were informed there were two for Ramsey 
unfortunately they do not have the transport to get from St Ives to Ramsey. Cllr J Clarke commented 
that there are always vehicles at the Huntingdon Police Station perhaps they could use them. Cllr R 
Terrill had suggested they use their own transport to get here and claim mileage. Cllr R Terrill was asked 
to follow this matter and report back to members. 
267. Meeting Dates 
 

The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council would take place on Thursday 23rd July 7pm (Planning).

Children from Ramsey Junior school and Ashbeach school attended and with the extra showing funded by Ramsey Town Council other groups including the Brownies attended meaning over 200 children had seen the show. Cllr C Maskell left the meeting at 8:20pm

• Cllr V Fendley had also attended the Ramsey Rotary handover and informed members that Chris Wick would be the President for this year. • Cllr V Fendley attended the Army Cadet showcase in Waterbeach, supporting the Ramsey Cadets and was disappointed no other Mayor’s supported their groups. • Cllr V Fendley attended AGE UK launch of Befriending Service in care homes. 60% of people in care homes do not receive visitors. This was held at Magnolia Park. • Cllr R Terrill and Cllr V Fendley attended the online Police meeting with Inspector Colin Norden. When challenged about the lack of PCSO’s for Ramsey they were informed there were two for Ramsey unfortunately they do not have the transport to get from St Ives to Ramsey. Cllr J Clarke commented that there are always vehicles at the Huntingdon Police Station perhaps they could use them. Cllr R Terrill had suggested they use their own transport to get here and claim mileage. Cllr R Terrill was asked to follow this matter and report back to members. 267. Meeting Dates
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council would take place on Thursday 23rd July 7pm (Planning).

 July as a true record.

MINUTES OF RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL MEETING 
held at 7pm on Thursday 9 July 2026 at  
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey 
 
 
Present:  Councillors: A Austin, I Axelsen, J Bufton, J Clarke, M Clarke, S Corney (Dep 
Mayor), V Fendley (Mayor), S Fice, C Maskell, R Terrill and L Webster. 
In attendance: Mrs L Renfree, Town Clerk  
 
254. Apologies for Absence. 
Cllrs J Aubin, J Clarke, L Knight, P Rose, and E Welsh. The Clerk informed members that Cllr 
Rebecca Cope had sent in by email her resignation that afternoon. 
 
Cllr V Fendley welcomed Cllr L Webster to her first Full Council meeting. 
  
255.To Receive Declarations of Interest. 
There were no Declarations of Interest. 
 
256. Public Participation. 
There were two members of the public present. 
 
257. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved. 
Having  been proposed  by  Cllr  S  Corney  and  seconded  by  Cllr  M  Clarke,  Council voted 10 
FOR and 1  ABSTENTION for the  Minutes  of  the  meeting  of  25th  June  2026  as  a  correct 
record. 
 
258.  District  Councillor  Update. Cllrs  H  Tobias,  K  Maheshwari  and  R  Coogan  had  been 
invited to address Town Council Members.  
Cllr K Maheshwari had put in his apologies, but no apologies were received by Cllr H Tobias 
or Cllr R Coogan. 
The Clerk read an email report from K Maheshwari  
‘Although I am unable to attend this meeting, I would like to provide a brief update. 
I continue to hold regular meetings with constituents and remain accessible by email and 
through my social media channels, ensuring residents can contact me whenever they need 
assistance. 
Where issues raised by residents require the involvement of Ramsey Town Council, I copy 
the Town Council into the relevant correspondence so that matters can be dealt with 
collaboratively. 
Since the last Town Council meeting, no issues have been referred to me by Ramsey Town 
Council that require an update. However, I remain available to assist the Town Council, 
fellow councillors and residents whenever support is needed. Please do not hesitate to 
contact me if there are any district council matters on which I can help. 
Thank you, and I look forward to continuing to work together for the benefit of Ramsey and 
the surrounding communities. 
Thanks 
Kind regards 
Cllr Karan Maheshwari 
Council members were very disappointed that there was no District Councillor present to 
represent Huntingdonshire District Council and asked the Clerk to raise this with them. 
Further feedback was that in Cllr Maheshwari report he stated he had not been asked to do 
any work on behalf of Ramsey Town Council, Cllr S Corney reminded members that he been 
asked to speak to Huntingdonshire District Council about the land at the back of the Doctors 
Surgery on Mews Close, and that Cllr S Corney had spoken to him at length after the 
meeting about the project and how to approach the Officers. It was also commented that Cllr 

2 
 
K Maheshwari had been promoting all local events and had not promoted the 4
th
 July Party 
in the Park a Town Council event. The Clerk had been asked to correspond with the three 
District Councillors for clarity on these issues and to gain commitment for future meetings. 
 
259. Planning Applications for Consideration 
1.1  26/01152/OUT Proposed  outline  application  for  development  of  up  to  19  residential 
dwellings  with  matters  committed  to  access.  Hankins  Garage  46  Whytefield  Road.  Ramsey 
PE26 1AH.After a lengthy discussion Proposed by Cllr L Webster and seconded by Cllr S Fice 
Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the outline 
plan but wanted the following comments to be noted for further plans.  
Ramsey Town Council members suggested the following: 
• having a lesser number of houses on the plot and increase the number of car parking 
spaces.  
• To have allocated visitor parking to take pressure away from Whytefield Road.  
• Have concerns where the flow of the attenuation pond would flow to 
• Suggest bungalow housing maybe preferable and take pressure away from parking 
spaces required. 
• There is a strip of land that goes from the site to Blenheim Road and even though it is 
outside of the application boundary was assurance this would not be used for traffic. 
• Council felt the application should make S106 and CIL contribution. 
260. Planning Other Business 
a) TRO – pedestrianisation – The Clerk informed members that the TRO was now being looked 
at by Cambridgeshire Highways and work should start in September. 
b) Street Naming to be noted. Static Caravan, Land Southeast of True Briton, Middle Drove, 
Ramsey Heights to be known as Hare’s Place - Noted 
c) Cllr V Fendley informed members that Huntingdonshire District Council had appointed the 
Independent Assessor for the Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan and they had 
started to ask questions which Anthony Northcote the Planning Advisor was answering. Cllr J 
Clarke asked if the answers would go through Ramsey Town Council, Cllr V Fendley 
reminded Members that the Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan Steering Group 
would be overseeing the process. 
 
261. Finance Items. 
a) Financial Summary – Cashbook to 30/06/2026 which was tabled. Noted. 
b) Expenditure Transactions to be approved. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by 
Cllr A Austin Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the expenditure transactions 
to be APPROVED 
c) The Clerk informed Members that the invoice had been received from Ramsey 
Neighbourhoods Trust for £3750. Cllr I Axelsen declared a non-pecuniary interest in this item 
as Chair of Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust and would not vote. After a discussion on how the 
youth provision was improving it was Proposed by Cllr S Fice and seconded by Cllr M Clarke 
Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION for the Clerk to pay the invoice. 
 
262. Working Party Recommendations. 
Cemetery Working Party 
For Council to agree to explore the option of having green burials in the Cemetery 
Extension, working in partnership with Muchwood. Cllr M Clarke informed members of the 
discussion that had taken place with herself, Cllr A Costello, Chris from Muchwood and the 
Clerk. The recommendation was for the Cemetery Working Party to look further into 
partnership working with Muchwood for a Green Burial Site on the extension section of the 
Wood Lane Cemetery. Proposed by Cllr M Clarke and seconded by Cllr A Costello, Ramsey 

3 
 
Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the Cemetery Working Party to continue to explore 
the opportunity for partnership working and feed back to Full Council. 
Cllr M Clarke handed over to Cllr A Costello for an update on the Mortuary Chapel. 
Cllr A Costello informed members that she had met with Nick Armour from Huntingdonshire 
District Council Conservation Team. The most urgent part of the restoration was to remove 
the glass of the contagion windows. Cllr A Costello had been contacting glass companies 
but there was a resistance to do the work. Cllr S Corney had passed on a contact who is 
prepared to do the work and is a Carpenter and Glazier, within the previously agreed limit 
and using the money donated by the Friends of the Mortuary Chapel the Clerk had engaged 
Sean Bellamy at a cost of £600 to remove the glass. 
Nick Armour also said to Councillor A Costello that with the plans the Town Council had for 
the site we should explore using Huntingdonshire District Council CIL funds. 
 
263. Abuse towards Council Employees and Ramsey Town Councillors. 
Ramsey Town Council Members had been made aware of a known individual who had been 
targeting the Town Clerk with verbal abuse, this person had also been abusive toward other 
Councillors and members of the public. This is now being investigated by Cambridgeshire 
Police. Cllr A Austin reminded the Clerk that if she requires immediate support to call the 
Emergency What’s App and a member would come to support. The Clerk along with council 
staff have access to a panic button as part of the Lone Working Policy. It was agreed the 
situation would be monitored. 
 
264. TOWN MAYOR’S AND CLERK’S CORRESPONDENCE: 
a) Cllr H Tobias email to the Clerk and response – Council to consider if any further 
comments are required – letter previously circulated. The Clerk had previously circulated an 
email and response that she had received from Huntingdonshire District Councillor for 
Ramsey Cllr Howard Tobias. The Clerk was instructed to write a further letter to Cllr H 
Tobais explaining the legislation that Town Council follow and cannot raise funds for other 
public bodies, to advise Cllr H Tobias to have a meeting with the Police and Crime 
Commissioner Daryl Preston who can influence where funds are spent on Policing. The 
Clerk was also asked to reiterate that the offer to use the facilities of Ramsey Town Council, 
the library was still available and to explore the use of the Ramsey Fire Station. 
 
b) Parking on Abbey Road. The Clerk informed Council that residents of Abbey Road had 
expressed concern over the parking plans at Abbey College. They were currently suffering 
from excess parking outside their properties and wanted to know what they could do. The 
Clerk had spoken with them and given advice. Cllr J Clarke did not think the road was 
private as the council had adopted the road from Hollow Lane to the Last house. Cllr J 
Bufton thought the bus turn around and the road to the school could be private and belong to 
the school. Cllr J Bufton suggested we note the residents’ comments but knowing that there 
will always have parking in Abbey Road because the school shut the gates for a short period 
of time each day.  
 
265. Freedom of Information Request from Ramsey Town Council 
FOI received from Huntingdonshire District Council this had previously been circulated to 
members and whilst they were disappointed in the response no further action would take 
place at this time. 
FOI Cambridgeshire Police – a response had now been received and would be circulated to 
members. 
 
266. ATTENDANCES AT MEETINGS AND ORGANISATIONS: 
• Cllr V Fendley and Cllr R Terrill had attended the Bishop of Ely’s Garden Party, a 
lovely event and was able to meet many other dignitaries from Cambridgeshire. 

4 
 
• The Clerk fed back from the 4
th
 July event, saying the feedback was, more please, 
and that ideas had been given for future event. 
• Cllr V Fendley fed back on a meeting she had attended online with Michelle Sacks 
CEO of Huntingdonshire District Council. Elections for the shadow authorities will 
take place next May. There is not an appeal process but if the authority had a strong 
case it could go to judicial review, or they could ask for some boundary amendments. 
The transition will still happen in May 2028. Regarding selling of Community Assets, 
they must still follow process and not sell the assets cheaply as it could impact the 
new Unitary. CIL can still be awarded even if it is for a future project and the funds 
can be ring-fenced. 
• Cllr C Maskell fed back about how well the Bands on the Green had been, each 
week had seen more than one hundred plus residents of all ages. 
• Cllr S Fice had attended the Ramsey St Mary’s PCC Strawberry Tea, which helps 
raise funds towards keeping the church open. 
• Cllr V Fendley informed members that the Project team had appointed Retail Revival 
to put together two business plans; one would be if Council was operating and one if 
it was operated through a social enterprise. 
•  Cllr V Fendley and the Clerk attended the Ramsey Junior School Eco Day and gave 
away previously prepared envelopes of wildflower seed by the Council staff team for 
the children to spread in their gardens. 
• Cllr V Fendley thanked the Council for supporting Once Upon a Time in Fenland 
which took place at Ramsey Rural Museum. Children from Ramsey Junior school 
and Ashbeach school attended and with the extra showing funded by Ramsey Town 
Council other groups including the Brownies attended meaning over 200 children had 
seen the show. 
           Cllr C Maskell left the meeting at 8:20pm 
 
• Cllr V Fendley had also attended the Ramsey Rotary handover and informed 
members that Chris Wick would be the President for this year. 
• Cllr V Fendley attended the Army Cadet showcase in Waterbeach, supporting the 
Ramsey Cadets and was disappointed no other Mayor’s supported their groups. 
• Cllr V Fendley attended AGE UK launch of Befriending Service in care homes. 60% 
of people in care homes do not receive visitors. This was held at Magnolia Park. 
• Cllr R Terrill and Cllr V Fendley attended the online Police meeting with Inspector 
Colin Norden. When challenged about the lack of PCSO’s for Ramsey they were 
informed there were two for Ramsey unfortunately they do not have the transport to 
get from St Ives to Ramsey. Cllr J Clarke commented that there are always vehicles 
at the Huntingdon Police Station perhaps they could use them. Cllr R Terrill had 
suggested they use their own transport to get here and claim mileage. Cllr R Terrill 
was asked to follow this matter and report back to members. 
267. Meeting Dates 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council would take place on Thursday 23rd July 7pm 
(Planning).

paragraphs: MINUTES OF RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL MEETING held at 7pm on Thursday 9 July 2026 at Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey
Present:  Councillors: A Austin, I Axelsen, J Bufton, J Clarke, M Clarke, S Corney (Dep Mayor), V Fendley (Mayor), S Fice, C Maskell, R Terrill and L Webster. In attendance: Mrs L Renfree, Town Clerk
254. Apologies for Absence. Cllrs J Aubin, J Clarke, L Knight, P Rose, and E Welsh. The Clerk informed members that Cllr Rebecca Cope had sent in by email her resignation that afternoon.
Cllr V Fendley welcomed Cllr L Webster to her first Full Council meeting.
255.To Receive Declarations of Interest. There were no Declarations of Interest.
256. Public Participation. There were two members of the public present.

257. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved. Having  been proposed  by  Cllr  S  Corney  and  seconded  by  Cllr  M  Clarke,  Council voted 10 FOR and 1  ABSTENTION for the  Minutes  of  the  meeting  of  25th  June  2026  as  a  correct record.

258.  District  Councillor  Update. Cllrs  H  Tobias,  K  Maheshwari  and  R  Coogan  had  been invited to address Town Council Members. Cllr K Maheshwari had put in his apologies, but no apologies were received by Cllr H Tobias or Cllr R Coogan. The Clerk read an email report from K Maheshwari ‘Although I am unable to attend this meeting, I would like to provide a brief update. I continue to hold regular meetings with constituents and remain accessible by email and through my social media channels, ensuring residents can contact me whenever they need assistance. Where issues raised by residents require the involvement of Ramsey Town Council, I copy the Town Council into the relevant correspondence so that matters can be dealt with collaboratively. Since the last Town Council meeting, no issues have been referred to me by Ramsey Town Council that require an update. However, I remain available to assist the Town Council, fellow councillors and residents whenever support is needed. Please do not hesitate to contact me if there are any district council matters on which I can help. Thank you, and I look forward to continuing to work together for the benefit of Ramsey and the surrounding communities. Thanks Kind regards Cllr Karan Maheshwari Council members were very disappointed that there was no District Councillor present to represent Huntingdonshire District Council and asked the Clerk to raise this with them. Further feedback was that in Cllr Maheshwari report he stated he had not been asked to do any work on behalf of Ramsey Town Council, Cllr S Corney reminded members that he been asked to speak to Huntingdonshire District Council about the land at the back of the Doctors Surgery on Mews Close, and that Cllr S Corney had spoken to him at length after the meeting about the project and how to approach the Officers. It was also commented that Cllr

K Maheshwari had been promoting all local events and had not promoted the 4 th July Party in the Park a Town Council event. The Clerk had been asked to correspond with the three District Councillors for clarity on these issues and to gain commitment for future meetings.

259. Planning Applications for Consideration 1.1  26/01152/OUT Proposed  outline  application  for  development  of  up  to  19  residential dwellings  with  matters  committed  to  access.  Hankins  Garage  46  Whytefield  Road.  Ramsey PE26 1AH.After a lengthy discussion Proposed by Cllr L Webster and seconded by Cllr S Fice Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to APPROVE the outline plan but wanted the following comments to be noted for further plans. Ramsey Town Council members suggested the following: • having a lesser number of houses on the plot and increase the number of car parking spaces. • To have allocated visitor parking to take pressure away from Whytefield Road. • Have concerns where the flow of the attenuation pond would flow to • Suggest bungalow housing maybe preferable and take pressure away from parking spaces required. • There is a strip of land that goes from the site to Blenheim Road and even though it is outside of the application boundary was assurance this would not be used for traffic. • Council felt the application should make S106 and CIL contribution. 260. Planning Other Business a) TRO – pedestrianisation – The Clerk informed members that the TRO was now being looked at by Cambridgeshire Highways and work should start in September. b) Street Naming to be noted. Static Caravan, Land Southeast of True Briton, Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights to be known as Hare’s Place - Noted c) Cllr V Fendley informed members that Huntingdonshire District Council had appointed the Independent Assessor for the Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan and they had started to ask questions which Anthony Northcote the Planning Advisor was answering. Cllr J Clarke asked if the answers would go through Ramsey Town Council, Cllr V Fendley reminded Members that the Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan Steering Group would be overseeing the process.

261. Finance Items. a) Financial Summary – Cashbook to 30/06/2026 which was tabled. Noted. b) Expenditure Transactions to be approved. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr A Austin Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the expenditure transactions to be APPROVED c) The Clerk informed Members that the invoice had been received from Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust for £3750. Cllr I Axelsen declared a non-pecuniary interest in this item as Chair of Ramsey Neighbourhoods Trust and would not vote. After a discussion on how the youth provision was improving it was Proposed by Cllr S Fice and seconded by Cllr M Clarke Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION for the Clerk to pay the invoice.

262. Working Party Recommendations. Cemetery Working Party For Council to agree to explore the option of having green burials in the Cemetery Extension, working in partnership with Muchwood. Cllr M Clarke informed members of the discussion that had taken place with herself, Cllr A Costello, Chris from Muchwood and the Clerk. The recommendation was for the Cemetery Working Party to look further into partnership working with Muchwood for a Green Burial Site on the extension section of the Wood Lane Cemetery. Proposed by Cllr M Clarke and seconded by Cllr A Costello, Ramsey

Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the Cemetery Working Party to continue to explore the opportunity for partnership working and feed back to Full Council. Cllr M Clarke handed over to Cllr A Costello for an update on the Mortuary Chapel. Cllr A Costello informed members that she had met with Nick Armour from Huntingdonshire District Council Conservation Team. The most urgent part of the restoration was to remove the glass of the contagion windows. Cllr A Costello had been contacting glass companies but there was a resistance to do the work. Cllr S Corney had passed on a contact who is prepared to do the work and is a Carpenter and Glazier, within the previously agreed limit and using the money donated by the Friends of the Mortuary Chapel the Clerk had engaged Sean Bellamy at a cost of £600 to remove the glass. Nick Armour also said to Councillor A Costello that with the plans the Town Council had for the site we should explore using Huntingdonshire District Council CIL funds.

263. Abuse towards Council Employees and Ramsey Town Councillors. Ramsey Town Council Members had been made aware of a known individual who had been targeting the Town Clerk with verbal abuse, this person had also been abusive toward other Councillors and members of the public. This is now being investigated by Cambridgeshire Police. Cllr A Austin reminded the Clerk that if she requires immediate support to call the Emergency What’s App and a member would come to support. The Clerk along with council staff have access to a panic button as part of the Lone Working Policy. It was agreed the situation would be monitored.

264. TOWN MAYOR’S AND CLERK’S CORRESPONDENCE: a) Cllr H Tobias email to the Clerk and response – Council to consider if any further comments are required – letter previously circulated. The Clerk had previously circulated an email and response that she had received from Huntingdonshire District Councillor for Ramsey Cllr Howard Tobias. The Clerk was instructed to write a further letter to Cllr H Tobais explaining the legislation that Town Council follow and cannot raise funds for other public bodies, to advise Cllr H Tobias to have a meeting with the Police and Crime Commissioner Daryl Preston who can influence where funds are spent on Policing. The Clerk was also asked to reiterate that the offer to use the facilities of Ramsey Town Council, the library was still available and to explore the use of the Ramsey Fire Station.

b) Parking on Abbey Road. The Clerk informed Council that residents of Abbey Road had expressed concern over the parking plans at Abbey College. They were currently suffering from excess parking outside their properties and wanted to know what they could do. The Clerk had spoken with them and given advice. Cllr J Clarke did not think the road was private as the council had adopted the road from Hollow Lane to the Last house. Cllr J Bufton thought the bus turn around and the road to the school could be private and belong to the school. Cllr J Bufton suggested we note the residents’ comments but knowing that there will always have parking in Abbey Road because the school shut the gates for a short period of time each day.

265. Freedom of Information Request from Ramsey Town Council FOI received from Huntingdonshire District Council this had previously been circulated to members and whilst they were disappointed in the response no further action would take place at this time. FOI Cambridgeshire Police – a response had now been received and would be circulated to members.

266. ATTENDANCES AT MEETINGS AND ORGANISATIONS: • Cllr V Fendley and Cllr R Terrill had attended the Bishop of Ely’s Garden Party, a lovely event and was able to meet many other dignitaries from Cambridgeshire.

• The Clerk fed back from the 4 th July event, saying the feedback was, more please, and that ideas had been given for future event. • Cllr V Fendley fed back on a meeting she had attended online with Michelle Sacks CEO of Huntingdonshire District Council. Elections for the shadow authorities will take place next May. There is not an appeal process but if the authority had a strong case it could go to judicial review, or they could ask for some boundary amendments. The transition will still happen in May 2028. Regarding selling of Community Assets, they must still follow process and not sell the assets cheaply as it could impact the new Unitary. CIL can still be awarded even if it is for a future project and the funds can be ring-fenced. • Cllr C Maskell fed back about how well the Bands on the Green had been, each week had seen more than one hundred plus residents of all ages. • Cllr S Fice had attended the Ramsey St Mary’s PCC Strawberry Tea, which helps raise funds towards keeping the church open. • Cllr V Fendley informed members that the Project team had appointed Retail Revival to put together two business plans; one would be if Council was operating and one if it was operated through a social enterprise. •  Cllr V Fendley and the Clerk attended the Ramsey Junior School Eco Day and gave away previously prepared envelopes of wildflower seed by the Council staff team for the children to spread in their gardens. • Cllr V Fendley thanked the Council for supporting Once Upon a Time in Fenland which took place at Ramsey Rural Museum. Children from Ramsey Junior school and Ashbeach school attended and with the extra showing funded by Ramsey Town Council other groups including the Brownies attended meaning over 200 children had seen the show. Cllr C Maskell left the meeting at 8:20pm

• Cllr V Fendley had also attended the Ramsey Rotary handover and informed members that Chris Wick would be the President for this year. • Cllr V Fendley attended the Army Cadet showcase in Waterbeach, supporting the Ramsey Cadets and was disappointed no other Mayor’s supported their groups. • Cllr V Fendley attended AGE UK launch of Befriending Service in care homes. 60% of people in care homes do not receive visitors. This was held at Magnolia Park. • Cllr R Terrill and Cllr V Fendley attended the online Police meeting with Inspector Colin Norden. When challenged about the lack of PCSO’s for Ramsey they were informed there were two for Ramsey unfortunately they do not have the transport to get from St Ives to Ramsey. Cllr J Clarke commented that there are always vehicles at the Huntingdon Police Station perhaps they could use them. Cllr R Terrill had suggested they use their own transport to get here and claim mileage. Cllr R Terrill was asked to follow this matter and report back to members. 267. Meeting Dates The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council would take place on Thursday 23rd July 7pm (Planning).

RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL 
 
You are hereby summoned to attend a meeting of Ramsey Town Council to be held in The Lavender Room, 
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey on Thursday 27 August 2026 at 7.00pm, when the following 
items of business will be transacted: - 
 
 
Please ensure all mobile phones are switched off or turned to silent during the meeting. 
 
A G E N D A  
   APOLOGIES FOR ABSENCE 
 
1. DECLARATIONS OF INTEREST 
To receive declarations from Members as to disclosable pecuniary and other interests and the nature of 
those interests in relation to any agenda item. 
   
2. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION 
To allow 20 minutes for any members of the public to address the Council.  
 
3. MINUTES 
To approve as a correct record, the Minutes of the meeting of the Council held on 13th August 2026 – 
attached. 
 
4. PLANNING 
1.1 26/01416/HHFUL – Erection of two storey extension, barn and carport, internal and external 
alterations, new dormer and canopy roofs and installation of solar PV panels. – Heathfield, Benwick 
Road, Ramsey Forty Foot, Huntingdon. 
1.2 26/01206/OUT- Proposed demolition of an existing dwelling and outbuilding and replacement with 4 
new dwellings (outline application with all matters reserved, with the exception of access) – 190 
Herne Road, Ramsey St Marys. 
1.3 26/01484/TREE – G1 (dead Silver Birch) - fell and remove – Cedar Lodge, St Marys Road, Ramsey 
St Marys. 
 
5. CONSULTATION ON THE REVIEWED BURY DRAFT NEIGHBOURHOOD PLAN 
Ramsey Town Council comments to be agreed. 
 
6. UPDATE ON EMERGENCY RESPONSE – HOLME FEN 
 
 
 
Would Cllrs please make time to look at the planning items on the District Council’s website 
before the meeting by accessing the HDC planning portal.  
  
  
7. MEETING DATES 
The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council will take place at 7pm on 10th September 2026.  
 
 
 Lisa Renfree                           21st August 2026 
     
      Town Clerk 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
MINUTES OF RAMSEY TOWN COUNCIL MEETING 
held at 7pm on Thursday 13 August 2026 at  
Ramsey Town Council Great Whyte, Ramsey 
 
 
Present:  Councillors: I Axelsen, J Clarke, M Clarke, S Corney (Dep Mayor), A Costello, V Fendley (Mayor), L Knight, C 
Maskell, R Terrill, L Webster, and E Welsh. 
In attendance: Mrs L Renfree, Town Clerk  
274. Apologies for Absence. 
Cllrs J Aubin, A Austin, J Bufton, S Fice, and P Rose. 
 
275.To Receive Declarations of Interest. 
No declarations of interest were received. 
 
276. Public Participation. 
There were 10 members of the public present. 
 
277. Minutes of the Last Meeting to be Approved. 
To  approve  as  a  correct  record,  the  minutes  of  the  meeting  Council  held  on  23rd  July  2026,  previously circulated. 
Proposed  by  Cllr  S  Corney  and  seconded  by  Cllr  R  Terrill  Ramsey  Town  Council  voted UNANIMOUSLY to  accept  the 
minutes of 23rd July as a true record. 
 
278. Co-option of New Town Councillor. 
Three  candidates  put  themselves  forward  for  co-option,  each  applicant  addressed  the  members  giving  an  overview  of 
themselves  and  why  they  felt  they  would  be  a  good  addition  to  the  Town  Council.  The  members  voted  and  Jessie 
Thompson received the most votes and would join the council at their August planning meeting. 
 
279. District and County Councillor Update: 
Cllrs Coogan, Maheshwari and Tobias were invited to update members of District and County Council matters, apologies 
received  from  Cllr  R  Coogan,  and  a  report tabled to  members. No  apologies  from  Cllr  Maheshwari.  Cllr  Tobias  reported 
back in person at the meeting as follows: Cllr Tobias informed members that he does not use social media to conduct his 
council  business  both  at  District  and  County  level  and  is  looking  to  work  in  collaboration  with  the  council and  residents, 
listening  and  challenging  to  make  the  Ramsey  ward  a  better  place  to  be.  Since  the  Huntingdonshire  District  Council 
meeting Cllr Tobias had been looking into the parking assessment and challenging the fact there is no business case for 
spending £370,000 of taxpayer’s money. Cllr Tobias informed members that some Ramsey plans were being discussed at 
the next Development Management Committee meeting. Cllr Tobias was happy to support CIL (Community Infrastructure 
Levy) applications if they will support the wider community. From a County Council perspective Cllr Tobias had been in the 
role  for  28  days  and  had  planned  to  meet  Highways  looking  at  the  road  infrastructure  and  is  looking  at  the  Student  Bus 
situation  where  the  decision  was  made  by  the  Peterborough  College.  The  Clerk  was  asked  to  communicate  with  Cllr 
Tobias to continue the work asked of Cllr Maheshwari on securing the land for the car park on Mews Close. 
 
 
 
280. Planning Applications for Consideration 
1.1 26/01128/LBC – Injection  of  a  SecoMUR  chemical  damp  proof  course  into  drilled  holes  to  all  external  walls  and  solid 
brick internal walls- Bridge Farm 15 Ramsey Road, Ramsey Forty Foot. Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr M 
Clarke Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for Huntingdonshire District Council to APPROVE the application. 
1.2 26/01328/HHFUL – Replacement of damaged cladding to front, side and rear of the property- 17 Wyatt Close, Ramsey. 
Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by L Webster Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for Huntingdonshire 
District Council to APPROVE the application, there was neighbouring support for the application, and  it is  in keeping  with 
the area. 
1.3 26/01385/FUL- Change of use of land from agricultural to residential curtilage associated with Kingfisher House – 
Kingfisher House, Whittlesey Road, Benwick, March. Proposed by Cllr C Maskell and seconded by Cllr J Clarke Ramsey 
Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for Huntingdonshire District Council to APPROVE the application. 
1.4 26/01352/FUL – Change of use of land to a gypsy and traveller residential pitch comprising the siting of one 
mobile home, one amenity building, associated hardstanding and ancillary works (part retrospective). – 
Land East of Fern Cottage, Harpers Drove, Ramsey Heights. The Clerk had received objections to the 
application from residents of Ramsey Heights as previously agreed with Huntingdonshire District Council. 
The Clerk was asked to submit to the planning portal their objections as laid out in the 21-page report 
previously circulated. Cllr A Costello proposed REFUSAL and Cllr seconded by Cllr L Webster Ramsey 
Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY for the District Council to REFUSE this application. The Clerk would 
also put the residents’ comments to the planning portal. 
 

281. Planning Other Business: 
a) Pedestrianisation update: Cllr V Fendley informed members that the TRO was live and that there would 
be a planning application being submitted for the shop in a box units. 
b) Abbey College LHI BID- The plans were out for consultation and Ramsey Town Council were asked if 
they wanted to add any further comments on the plan. Ramsey Town Council did not want to add any 
further comments. 
c) Consultation on the Reviewed Bury Village Draft Neighbourhood Plan – Cllr V Fendley talked through the 
Goals and Objectives from the Bury Village Neighbourhood Plan and informed members it would be on 
the agenda for the next planning meeting for comment. 
d) To note the Tree Preservation Order26/002 – Ramsey Rural Museum had been confirmed. Noted 
e) Notice of application for a Town/ Village Green, Abbey Green, Ramsey. Noted. 
f) Huntingdonshire District Council Local Plan Consultation – Members to agree to using Anthony Northcote 
for advice regarding Ramsey Town Council’s response. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr R 
Terrill Ramsey town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 AGAINST for the Clerk to instruct Anthony Northcote to 
give advice to Ramsey Town Council to comment on Huntingdonshire District Council’s Local Plan. 
282. Finance Items: 
a) Financial Summary – Cash book to 31/07/2026 tabled – Noted 
b) Expenditure Transactions to be approved – tabled- Proposed by Cllr S Corney and seconded by Cllr L 
Knight Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to agree the expenditure transactions. 
283. Working Part Recommendations: 
 Recommendations from the Economic Development Working Party 
a) For Ramsey Town Council to agree in principle to take control of the shop in a box units moving forward 
post successful TRO and Full Planning approval, and for Ramsey Town Council to manage the gated 
timings – Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR 
and 1 ABSTENTION for Ramsey Town Council to in principle take control of the Shop in a box units 
subject to a successful TRO and Full Planning approval. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr 
S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION for Ramsey Town Council to 
manage the gated timings. 
b) For Ramsey Town Council to initiate a Local Business Group to engage with our local businesses, with a 
view to sharing information. It was felt that a communication streamline to all Ramsey Parish Businesses 
was lacking and that this meeting would bring them together to explore a process moving forward. 
Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY 
for a business meeting to be arranged in September. 
Recommendations from the Amenities, Highways, Health, and Leisure Working Party. 
a) For Ramsey Town Council to decide between two quotes for the Public Toilet Doors both quotes ex vat.

an amendment to the cost of the Healthmatic quote £10,050. Proposed by Cllr A Costello and seconded 
by Cllr C Maskell Ramsey Town Council voted UNANIMOUSLY to accept the quote from LAM 
Automation LTD at a cost of £8,660.00 and the funds would come from the CIL account.  
b) For Ramsey Town Council to decide if they want the public toilet doors to have windows in them at a cost 
of £700 ex vat. Proposed by Cllr J Clarke and seconded by Cllr C Maskell to REFUSE the windows in the 
public toilet doors. Ramsey Town Council voted REFUSE 6 and 3 AGAINST 2 ABSTENTIONS for the 
public toilets to not have windows. 
c) For Ramsey Town Council to agree in principle a large mural sited at the QEII Skatepark. Final design to 
be voted on in the future. - paper circulated. After a long discussion on the subject, it was agreed 
UNANIMOUSLY for the proposal to go back to Amenities, Highways, Health & Leisure for further 
exploration. 
Recommendations from the Communications Working Party. 
      a) To Agree the draft Digital Screen Policy for Ramsey Town Council previously                                                                                       
circulated. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 
ABSTENTION to APPROVE the Digital Screen Policy. 
a) To Agree the Risk Assessment for Public Meetings at Ramsey Town Council- previously 
circulated. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney. Ramsey Town Council 
voted 9 FOR and 2 ABSTENTIONS to APPROVE the Risk Assessment for Public Meetings. 
b) To Agree the Risk Assessment for Premises and Buildings- previously circulated. Proposed by 
Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council vote 9 FOR and 2 
ABSTENTIONS to APPROVE the Risk Assessment for Premises and Buildings. 

c) To Review the current IT Policy – previously circulated. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded 
by Cllr S Corney Ramsey Town Council voted 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION to APPROVE the 
updated IT Policy. 
d) To agree the new email footer –tabled. Proposed by Cllr L Knight and seconded by Cllr S Corney 
Ramsey Town Council vote 10 FOR and 1 ABSTENTION to use the footer tabled for Councillor 
emails. The Clerk will circulate to members to use. 
284. WORKING PARTY UPDATE  
a) Members to receive an update from the Chair of each Working Party- previously circulated. Cllr L 
Knight said this was a very useful document and is a really good idea. The document was noted. 
 
285. FEEDBACK FROM GRANT FROM COMMUNITY SAFETY & SAFETY PARTNERSHIP. 
a) Feedback from Future Scooter Foundation -the Clerk showed two small video clips from some of 
the young people who participated in the evening event. There was a positive debate, and it was 
agreed that it would be good to have more young girls participating. Noted 
 
286. TOWN MAYOR’S AND CLERK’S CORRESPONDENCE:

investigation with Huntingdonshire District Council Anti-Social behaviour team. They are now 
looking to produce a Criminal Behaviour Order to protect the Council. 
b) Resident communication on noise from skate park and concerns RTC would put lighting there for 
after dark use. The Clerk informed members that a resident after reading a District Councillors 
post on having lighting at the Skatepark was very upset as Ramsey Town Council had said that 
would not be the case. Cllr Fendley was very clear that there would be no plans to light up the 
Skatepark. 
c) Resident communication on thanking the Town Council for the work Paul and Morgan are doing 
keeping the Cemetery clear and improving the area. The Clerk informed members that positive 
comments had been received about the work in clearing the Cemetery. 
d) Thank you from the Ramsey Garden and Horticulture Club for the grant we gave them which 
enable two new competitions this year. Cllr Fendley informed members of the letter received 
thanking Ramsey Town Council for their grant and the opportunities it has given their club. 
e) Ramsey Heights residents concern over lack of Fire Hydrant for the Droves. After the fire on 
Harpers Drove, residents were concerned that the Fire Service had to keep going away to refill 
the tanker. This was noted. 
Councillor Costello left the meeting at 8:55pm.

a) Safer Communities Public Meeting - Cllr V Fendley fed back on the public meeting held at 
Ramsey Forty Foot. Cllr V Fendley praised the Inspector for his honesty during the meeting, but 
the overall outcome was we do live in a safe community. 
b) Mayor met with County Councillor Cllr H Tobias. Cllr V Fendley informed members that she had 
had a meeting and discussed the LHI bids and infrastructure. 
c) Magnolia Park Opening Day- Cllr V Fendley attended the opening and it was a very positive day. 
d) Jones Court 40
th
 Anniversary BBQ – Cllr V Fendley and the Clerk attended the BBQ, and Cllr V 
Fendley had the difficult task of judging the baking competition. 
e) Update on correspondence with Cambridgeshire Constabulary – Cllr R Terrill updated members 
on his conversation with Inspector Norden. 
f) MP Sam Carling – Local Surgery Date 14
th
 August 2026. Cllr V Fendley informed members that 
the MP was in the community meeting with residents.

The next meeting of Ramsey Town Council (Planning) will take place on 27th August 2026 at 7pm.
